title: Devastating European wildfires in maps - and how they're being tackled
excerpt:
Wildfires are tearing through France and Spain, forcing more than 300,000 people to evacuate their homes.

France has seen its worst wildfires in two decades, while officials in the Spanish capital Ma...
body_text:
Wildfires are tearing through France and Spain, forcing more than 300,000 people to evacuate their homes.

France has seen its worst wildfires in two decades, while officials in the Spanish capital Madrid say the fires are the worst the region has ever experienced.

It follows a sweltering summer of heatwaves across Europe that have seen temperatures soar above 40C (104F) in many places.

Three separate wildfires in the mountains outside Madrid have together burned about 297 sq miles (770 sq km), authorities estimate - an area larger than Madrid itself.

In France, the worst affected area is Gironde, around the city of Bordeaux, where more than 200,000 people have been forced from their homes.

The blaze has spread rapidly, tearing through forests and fields in France's famous wine region, and burning more than 162 sq miles (420 sq km) in less than four days - an area roughly four times the size of Paris.

It is now just nine miles (15km) from the south of Bordeaux.

The fires have also threatened a number of sensitive military and industrial sites in the area, including facilities that work on French ballistic missiles, rocket motors, and the processing of hazardous chemicals.

Satellite imagery above Gironde shows vast areas of scorched, blackened earth, with smoke drifting inland to the east.

The fires have become so extreme they have created their own giant fire thunderstorm.

A rare weather event, storms like these are formed when heat from the wildfires makes the air above the fire rise rapidly, carrying smoke, ash and water vapour high into the atmosphere.

As the air rises, it cools, and the water vapour condenses into a cloud. If the fire is powerful enough and the atmosphere is unstable, that cloud can grow into a cumulonimbus - the same type of cloud associated with thunderstorms.

If these clouds then become large enough, they can produce their own lightning, which can then start new fires. They can also occasionally bring hail and rain.

These extreme and unpredictable conditions make the fires all the more difficult to stop.

To combat them, French firefighters have been using planes loaded with fire retardant, as well as planes like the Canadair, which can scoop 6,000 litres of water from lakes or the sea in 12 seconds and drop it directly on the fires.

On dangerous days, loaded aircraft patrol high-risk areas before any fires have been reported, so they can drop within minutes of a sighting. Planes often fly in a continuous shuttle while retardant is laid along the edges of the fire and ground crews attack the flames directly.

In Gironde, about 2,500 firefighters, 1,500 military personnel, and 1,200 police officers and gendarmes have been involved in tackling the blaze.

But even with these numbers, Gironde official Jean Luc Gleyze told the BBC that authorities don't have enough people to combat the fires.

"We don't have enough people and enough trucks and even I think France don't have enough," he said.

Around the town of Lacanau, bulldozers, diggers and mechanical shovels have been used to carve a firebreak that is 100m (328ft) wide at points, according to French media.

A firebreak is essentially a stretch of land that has been stripped of all vegetation to stop the fire from spreading - removing any potential fuel before the fire has a chance to reach it.

Spanish teams have been using many of the same techniques to tackle their wildfires, which are on course to become the worst the country has seen in two decades.

Francisco Martin, a government delegate in Madrid, described the fires as  "undoubtedly the largest fire in the history of the Madrid region".

This summer's fires have been aided by the hotter, drier conditions caused by climate change, which allow fires to spread faster and burn more fiercely.

Many on the ground - in both Spain and France - are fearful that the coming week could see worsening conditions, with high pressure forecast to bring dry, settled and increasingly hot temperatures.

The fires near Bordeaux are in an area popular with tourists

The region also borders the Atlantic ocean

The Gironde fires have torn through 162 sq miles in less than four days

Additional reporting by Elizabeth Rizzini and Helen Willetts

title: Fauci expressed disillusionment with ‘rambling, crazy’ Trump in journal
excerpt:
Former top US health official wrote about challenging interactions with publicity-fixated Trump during Covid

Diary entries released by a Republican senator in an attempt to damage Anthony Fauci also ...
body_text:
Former top US health official wrote about challenging interactions with publicity-fixated Trump during Covid

Diary entries released by a Republican senator in an attempt to damage Anthony Fauci also show the former top US government science adviser’s growing disillusionment with Donald Trump in the first year of the Covid-19 pandemic, branding the president “rambling”, “crazy”, “desperate”, “bumbling”, “incompetent”, “an idiot”, “a true embarrassment”, “totally nuts” and “truly an obnoxious adolescent”.

From the earliest days of the crisis six years ago, Fauci noted in his journal challenging interactions with the publicity-fixated Trump. On 27 February 2020, amid the first stirrings of public alarm, he wrote of a surprise late-night call, in which the US president “wanted to chat about the coronavirus situation in general”.

For “about 20-25 minutes”, Fauci wrote, he “encouraged [Trump] not to underplay the seriousness of the situation since if it turns out bad, it would look like he is covering up. I even spoke to him from a political standpoint that his chances for re-election might be more damaged if he downplayed the potential spread of virus in the USA than if he said we may face serious problems and even if the Stock Market goes down further, he was at least honest and the country would respect him for it.

“I thought that he heard what I said, but the next day, he again underplayed it.”

By 14 March, in the thick of the first Covid shutdowns, Fauci is bemoaning Trump’s fixation on “the fluff of ratings and publicity. And so he wants us to do 2 press conferences/day – one in AM and one in PM … We now will have no time to do work.”

On 22 May, Fauci wrote that Trump is “getting out of control in pushing to open up the country and get the economy back before election day. He is desparate [sic]. This is all about re-election.”

That proved correct. In October 2020, Fauci wrote: “As the [presidential] election nears, the cases increase and surges are inevitable as we enter cooler weather. Trump is on the campaign trail spewing nonsense. He is really out of control. A true embarrassment.”

By March 2021, having watched Trump attempt to retain power despite electoral defeat in a way that reminds him “historically of Hitler”, Fauci writes: “He is truly an obnoxious adolescent.”

Fauci’s diary entries read as raw source material for reporting on the pandemic and its politics. He admitted to being a source himself, and worried about being suspected as a leaker, but wrote in late May 2020: “Had long conversation on ‘background’ with [Washington Post reporter] Bob Woodward who is writing a book on the early response to Covid in the USA. I provided him with some history of our response in early January and into February. Will tlak [sic] more with him tomorow [sic].”

The release of Fauci’s diaries was orchestrated by Rand Paul, the Republican senator from Kentucky, who has long voiced skepticism about the Covid-19 response Fauci led, accusing him of needlessly shutting down the country while covering the supposed truth that the virus was human-made, and that US-funded research contributed to its creation. Fauci has consistently said the virus originated in animal-to-human transmission, the generally accepted theory.

The two men have clashed before. At a hearing in January 2022, for example, Fauci told Paul his attacks put him in danger, “kindl[ing] the crazies out there and I have threats upon my life, harassment of my family and my children with obscene phone calls because people are lying about me”. Fauci also charged: “You are making a catastrophic epidemic for your political gain.”

Paul and Fauci will square off again on Wednesday, at a hearing for which Fauci, 85, was compelled to appear. Paul has said he will “make sure Fauci answers for his dangerous decisions and the consequences they had for millions”.

In the rightwing press, coverage of the Fauci diaries has focused on his notes about his rise to global fame amid the Covid response, particularly about meeting celebrities or appearing on TV and in the press. The singer Joan Baez and actors Julia Roberts and Sean Penn are among names prominently noted.

Fauci does seem to have been proud of his newfound celebrity. On 13 July 2020, his relationship with Trump rapidly souring, he turned to his diary.

“Major, Major show of support for me for multiple and varied sectors,” he writes. “Most peo[p]le expressing outrage that the trump administration woud [sic] be so bumbling and incompetent to try to discredit the most credible scientist in the world.”

title: ABC, NBC, CBS, CNN and MS NOW ignore Fauci diary entries that reveal fixation on fame during COVID
excerpt:
Former Clinton NSC staff member Jamie Metzl joins Fox & Friends Weekend to discuss Dr. Anthony Faucis upcoming Senate hearing on the origins of COVID.

Eye-popping diary entries written by Dr. Anthony...
body_text:
Former Clinton NSC staff member Jamie Metzl joins Fox & Friends Weekend to discuss Dr. Anthony Faucis upcoming Senate hearing on the origins of COVID.

Eye-popping diary entries written by Dr. Anthony Fauci reveal the former White House COVID advisor was fixated on his newfound celebrity at the height of the global pandemic, but anyone who relies on legacy media outlets for news and information may not be aware.

ABC News, NBC News, CBS News, CNN and MS NOW's on-air broadcasts ignored Fauci’s diary entries from the time they were released on Saturday afternoon through Monday at 9 a.m. ET when flagship morning shows had concluded, according to a search of transcripts using Grabien Media.

Released by Senate Homeland Security Committee Chairman Rand Paul, R-Ky., the journals chronicle Fauci's day-to-day role during the COVID-19 crisis through conversations with President Donald Trump, governors and world leaders, media appearances, and his personal observations as the pandemic unfolded in 2020.

FAUCI'S NEWLY RELEASED COVID DIARIES REVEAL BIZARRE FIXATION ON FAME AS PANDEMIC DEATHS MOUNTED

Diary entries written by Dr. Anthony Fauci have been ignored by numerous media outlets on the airwaves. (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images)

Paul, a longtime Fauci critic who frequently clashed with him over the federal response and the origins of the virus, made the diaries public as part of the committee's ongoing oversight investigation. The diary entries document Fauci’s fondness of his newfound fame, cozy relationships with a variety of legacy media personalities, his growing frustration with the Trump White House and the suggestion that it was "not hyperbole" to say he was "the most famous and talked about person in the country."

The diary entries exploded on social media but appear to have been ignored by mainstream news networks.

"NBC Nightly News" failed to mention the story over the weekend and NBC continued to look the other way Monday morning on "Today," according to Grabien transcripts. On ABC, "World News Tonight" and "Good Morning America" followed the same pattern, while "CBS’ Evening News" and "CBS Mornings" didn’t find anything newsworthy, either.

Sunday affairs programs such as ABC’s "This Week," NBC’s "Meet the Press" and CBS’ "Face the Nation" also declined to cover Fauci’s diary.

INSIDE FAUCI'S PRIVATE DIARY: WHAT HE WROTE ABOUT TRUMP, TV PERSONALITIES AND CELEBRITIES

President Donald Trump listens to Dr. Anthony Fauci, the then-director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, speak with members of the coronavirus task force during a briefing on Friday, April 17, 2020, in Washington, DC. (Jabin Botsford/The Washington Post via Getty Images)

It was much of the same on cable news, as CNN and MS NOW both ignored the story on linear television through Monday morning. The word "Fauci" was not mentioned once, according to Grabien Media.

CNN’s on-air blackout came despite anchor Jake Tapper appearing repeatedly throughout the private diary entries as Fauci documented phone calls, text exchanges and dinners at the Tappers' Washington home amid their growing friendship.

Fauci wrote that Tapper privately checked to make sure a CNN interview hadn't caused problems with the White House. When The Atlantic's Peter Nicholas suggested Fauci had been "humiliated" over a canceled Tapper interview, Fauci fired back in his diary: "F--- you, Peter."

After Fauci's heated exchange with GOP Ohio Rep. Jim Jordan in April 2021, Fauci wrote that CNN's Dana Bash texted him, telling him he was "a better man" and relaying that fellow CNN anchor Wolf Blitzer had joked no one would have blamed Fauci if he had told Jordan to "go f--- yourself."

CONSERVATIVE GROUPS URGE FCC TO BACK OFF ABC LICENSE REVIEW, WARNING IT COULD HURT RIGHT-LEANING MEDIA

Diary entries written by Dr. Anthony Fauci shocked social media over the weekend.  (Getty Images)

Fox News chief political analyst Brit Hume took notice of the media blackout.

"This is not getting the coverage it deserves," Hume wrote on X. "Is that because so many media luminaries were so chummy with the man at the center of a major medical controversy?"

ABC, NBC, CBS and CNN did not immediately respond to a request for comment. MS NOW declined comment.

The diary release came days before Fauci is scheduled to testify before the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee after being subpoenaed by Paul. Several network insiders have suggested the news broke during a busy news cycle and there is still time to cover it before Wednesday’s hearing.

Fox News Digital’s Amanda Macias contributed to this report.

Brian Flood is a media editor/reporter for FOX News Digital. Story tips can be sent to brian.flood@fox.com and on Twitter: @briansflood.

title: Homeless families in London temporary housing told not to use air conditioning
excerpt:
Exclusive: Two children reportedly taken to hospital after residents told in-built units ‘not offered as amenity’

Homeless families placed in temporary accommodation in London were told they could no...
body_text:
Exclusive: Two children reportedly taken to hospital after residents told in-built units ‘not offered as amenity’

Homeless families placed in temporary accommodation in London were told they could not use the in-built air conditioning as it had “not been offered as an amenity” for them, leading to two children being hospitalised during recent heatwaves.

Some residents at Britannia Point in Colliers Wood, south-west London, experienced such stifling conditions that young children became ill. The company managing some of the tenancies involved told the Guardian households in temporary accommodation had now been told they could use the air conditioning.

However, some residents said they were informed that if they use the system they will be billed via a standing charge rather than for how long the air conditioning runs, which could result in bills of up to £500 for the entire summer.

The 19-storey glass-fronted block is owned by Criterion Capital, set up by the billionaire property magnate Asif Aziz. The company was accused earlier this year of trying to mass-evict tenants shortly before no-fault evictions were banned, something the company has denied.

The temporary accommodation tenancies, which see councils place otherwise homeless households in properties for periods that can last from weeks to years, are managed separately by lettings agencies, one of them London-based Aura Assets Management.

After a tenant complained to the building management about their air conditioning not working, they were sent an email, seen by the Guardian, which said that under the tenancy as managed by Aura, air conditioning “has been switched off” for households in emergency accommodation.

It went on: “Air conditioning has not been offered as an amenity under these arrangements, and the units cannot be switched back on as a result. You are welcome to use a portable fan or portable air conditioning unit at your own arrangement in the meantime.”

Residents say the all-glass construction of the block and the fact that windows open only slightly mean that, without air conditioning, their flats have become unbearably hot.

“It is very difficult to cool the flats down,” one resident said. “I find that as soon as I enter the building, I become much hotter, start feeling sick and sweat profusely.”

Alice Rogers, who lives in Britannia Point with her four-year-old son Hassan, said they regularly had to leave the block due to the heat. “There is a window that you can open, but there’s not much of a difference that makes,” she said. “Whether you open it or close it, it’s just literally the same.”

She added: “My son had a nosebleed the other day and was faint. I’m very much worried about his life.”

Stuart Neaverson, a Labour councillor in Merton who has been trying to assist residents along with the local MP, Labour’s Siobhain McDonagh, said he had been told about two children being taken to hospital because of the heat, calling the situation “disgraceful”.

He said: “With another heatwave imminent, it’s vital that air conditioning is restored immediately to everyone in the tower to help prevent a tragedy.”

A statement from Aura Assets Management said the air conditioning was now “fully operational and tenants have been advised that they are welcome to use it”. It went on: “Given the exceptionally warm weather this summer, we have also encouraged sensible, rather than continuous, use, simply to help residents avoid unexpectedly high utility bills – not to discourage use of a service that exists for their comfort.”

When asked about the email sent to a resident saying tenants in temporary accommodation were not given access to air conditioning, the company said in a subsequent statement that this “was issued by the building management based on the information and operational arrangements in place at the time”.

This email was sent to a “couple of flats”, the new statement said, adding: “The situation has since changed.”

Criterion has been contacted for comment.

title: Chile captures fugitive convicted of singer Victor Jara's murder under Pinochet
excerpt:
Victor Jara is still remembered decades later as a victim of the Pinochet regime

Police in Chile say they have captured a man convicted years ago of the kidnapping and murder of popular folk singer V...
body_text:
Victor Jara is still remembered decades later as a victim of the Pinochet regime

Police in Chile say they have captured a man convicted years ago of the kidnapping and murder of popular folk singer Victor Jara under military ruler Augusto Pinochet.

Nelson Haase was one of a group of officers given jail terms for the killing, which took place just five days after the coup which brought Pinochet to power in 1973. He was sentenced to 25 years.

Haase took flight when the sentence was announced in August 2023 but was found by police on Saturday in the south of the country.

Jara, who became famous in the 1960s and 70s for his protest and pacifist songs and supported the ousted socialist president Salvador Allende, was subjected to torture and shot 44 times.

He was one of about 5,000 people, arrested in the immediate aftermath of the coup, who were taken to a sports stadium in the capital.

Those who survived the ordeal recounted how the singer was tortured, with soldiers crushing his fingers and telling him he would never be able to play his guitar again.

His case is one of the most striking examples of how the Pinochet dictatorship dealt with its enemies.

Thousands were tortured, executed or disappeared during the 17-year regime.

Haase, a retired colonel, was one of eight officers found guilty of Jara's murder in 2018.

After five years of appeals, the country's Supreme Court made a final judgement in the case, sentencing Haase for 15 years for murder and another 10 for kidnapping.

The then 80-year-old failed to appear voluntarily to serve his sentence, and disappeared for nearly three years. Local media said he was found by police agents in Puyehue, in the Los Lagos region 950 km (590 miles) south of the capital Santiago on Saturday.

Another of the seven men convicted of murder, Gen Hernan Chacon, died by suicide when police came to arrest him. The remaining five are all in jail.

Also in 2023, the US extradited to Chile retired army lieutenant Pedro Barrientos, who a Florida jury had found liable for Jara's murder.

Víctor Jara: The folk singer murdered for his music

title: Britain braces for fourth heatwave of year as fire chiefs issue public appeal
excerpt:
Temperatures up to 35C forecast, triggering heat health alerts and pleas to take care in parched parks and rural areas

Paramedics and firefighters are braced for emergencies across the country this w...
body_text:
Temperatures up to 35C forecast, triggering heat health alerts and pleas to take care in parched parks and rural areas

Paramedics and firefighters are braced for emergencies across the country this week after UK forecasters predicted a fourth heatwave of the year.

Temperatures are forecast to reach as high as 35C by Wednesday, triggering heat health alerts and an appeal from fire chiefs to take care in parched parks and rural areas.

July has been 3C above average across the UK, according to provisional Met Office data, and with more than a month of summer left, the UK has already faced more days above 30C than ever before.

Southern England has had just 1% of its average July rainfall, while England as a whole has had 5% and the UK 20%, according to the Met Office.

Forecasters predict this latest heatwave will at least be shortlived. Temperatures are expected to rise from Tuesday, reaching 30C as a high pressure system sits across the east and south-east of the country, before the peak of the heat comes on Wednesday.

Temperatures would begin to gradually cool from Thursday, the Met Office said, except in the south-east where another hot day could keep the region in official heatwave conditions.

The heat was likely to have a significant impact on the health of vulnerable people and increase demand on health services, the UK Health Security Agency said on Monday, as it issued amber heat health alerts for the east and south-east of England.

They begin on Wednesday at 9am and end on Thursday. Yellow heat health alerts will remain in place for Yorkshire and the Humber, West Midlands and south-west regions for the same time period.

Ambulance and emergency medical teams anticipate a surge in patients suffering dehydration, heat exhaustion and heatstroke, as well as from patients with heart and respiratory illnesses that can be badly exacerbated by high temperatures.

“Recent episodes of extreme heat have shown how quickly patients can become seriously unwell,” said Helen Vine, the assistant director of the Association of Ambulance Chief Executives (AACE).

“With amber heat health alerts in place, we would urge people to take the risks seriously by staying hydrated, avoiding strenuous activity during the hottest parts of the day, limiting alcohol consumption and seeking advice from NHS 111 for non-emergency health concerns.”

With wildfires across Europe displacing hundreds of thousands of people in France and Spain in recent days, UK fire chiefs were also priming themselves for the possibility that the latest heatwave could increase the chance of further wildfires in the UK.

Residents of Nethy Bridge in Scotland had to be evacuated at the weekend after a large fire broke out in the Cairngorms national park. And at the height of the third heatwave in mid-July, firefighters were battling 19 significant wildfires simultaneously in England and Wales.

On Monday a spokesperson for the National Fire Chiefs Council urged the public to avoid using disposable barbecues in parks, the countryside and other green spaces, and to take care with cigarette butts. “It only takes one spark to start a wildfire, and what may appear to be a small fire can quickly escalate, threatening communities, wildlife, natural habitats and the firefighters tackling the incident.”

Human-caused climate breakdown is making every heatwave in the world more intense and more likely to happen. The sustained increase in temperatures may lead to a redefinition of the criteria for a heatwave. Heatwave thresholds for some counties were nudged up by a degree four or five years ago, said the senior Met Office meteorologist Marco Petagna.

“Going forward they’ll need to be adjusted to take into account … current climate, otherwise we’re going to more frequently go into heatwaves. It’s a moveable thing, really, as we go through a warming world.”

title: Oregon ballot measure that would have criminalized hunting and fishing fails to qualify for vote
excerpt: Fox News' Joey Jones reacts to a petition in Oregon to ban hunting and fishing, which has garnered 125,000 signatures. Jones argues that such bans overlook hunters' vital role in wildlife management a...
body_text:
Fox News' Joey Jones reacts to a petition in Oregon to ban hunting and fishing, which has garnered 125,000 signatures. Jones argues that such bans overlook hunters' vital role in wildlife management and animal conservation, and how animal existence often depends on human stewardship and ethical practices, rather than causing harm.

Oregon hunters, anglers and farmers can breathe a sigh of relief.

Initiative Petition 28 — the deceptively branded animal-rights proposal that would have effectively criminalized hunting, fishing, ranching and a long list of other normal activities — will not appear on Oregon’s November ballot after all.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK

A hunter wearing blaze orange and camouflage stands in a mountainous forest carrying a rifle while observing the landscape. (Getty Images)

Supporters of IP28 submitted more than 142,000 signatures, comfortably exceeding the 117,173 required to qualify for the ballot. But after two rounds of verification, the Oregon Secretary of State’s Office determined that only 104,262 of those signatures were valid.

That left the campaign roughly 13,000 signatures short.

Because while proponents called IP28 the People for the Elimination of Animal Cruelty Exemptions Act — or the warm and fuzzy-sounding "PEACE Act" — the proposal was never simply about prosecuting people who abuse animals. Oregon already has laws for that.

IP28 sought to remove the exemptions in Oregon’s animal-cruelty statutes that protect lawful hunting, fishing, trapping, ranching, farming, pest control and accepted animal-husbandry practices.

Under the proposal, killing or injuring an animal would have been classified as abuse unless it was necessary to prevent immediate harm to a person or another animal.

SPINY LOBSTER MINI SEASON KICKS OFF IN FLORIDA, DRAWING EAGER DIVERS TO THE WATER

That means hunters harvesting deer, anglers keeping fish, ranchers processing cattle, commercial fishermen bringing seafood to shore and farmers controlling pests could all have potentially faced criminal consequences.

Two farmers manage cattle in a pen during sunset in a rural landscape. (Getty Images)

The proposal was so extreme that opposing it became one of the few genuinely bipartisan causes left in American politics.

Oregon Gov. Tina Kotek, U.S. Sen. Jeff Merkley, all 37 Democrats in the Oregon House and Republican lawmakers across the state spoke out against it. The Oregon Farm Bureau, Oregon Veterinary Medical Association and Oregon Hunters Association also opposed the initiative.

Kotek said Friday that she was "relieved" IP28 failed to qualify.

"I know from conversations with Oregonians across the state that this measure would have done nothing to help them," she said.

IP28 would not have created some peaceful wildlife paradise where every deer, elk, fish, cow and invasive pest lived happily ever after. It would have undermined the very wildlife-management system that keeps animal populations and habitats healthy.

Hunters and anglers provide enormous amounts of conservation funding through license sales and federal excise taxes on firearms, ammunition, archery equipment and fishing gear. Those dollars help states acquire habitat, maintain boat ramps, conduct wildlife research, restore species and operate public recreation programs used by everyone.

Travis Thompson, a conservation advocate who helped lead the successful effort to establish a constitutional right to hunt and fish in Florida, recently explained to OutKick Outdoors that sportsmen’s contributions support far more than hunting and fishing.

"It’s used to acquire lands. It’s used for boat-ramp maintenance. It’s used for youth programs. It’s used for all sorts of things that everyone benefits from," Thompson said. "The places where I hunt aren’t just limited to me hunting. There are people who bike on them, ride horses, walk their dogs, hike or bird-watch."

Watch Travis Thompson's full interview with OutKick Outdoors here:

Eliminating hunting and fishing would not eliminate the need for wildlife management, either. It would simply transfer the cost from sportsmen to taxpayers — assuming the state continued managing wildlife at all.

Without regulated hunting, growing wildlife populations can lead to habitat destruction, disease, starvation, crop damage and more vehicle collisions. Invasive species would create another obvious problem, since IP28 did not include a broad exemption allowing them to be removed before they devastated native ecosystems.

As Thompson put it, wildlife policy must be driven by science rather than "emotions or feelings."

That is exactly why the defeat of IP28 matters beyond Oregon.

Across the country, hunters, anglers and conservation groups are fighting two related battles. In some states, activists are attempting to restrict hunting, fishing, trapping, the use of live bait and other traditional outdoor activities. In others, sportsmen are trying to pass constitutional protections recognizing the right to hunt and fish.

Florida became the 24th state to adopt such a protection when voters approved Amendment 2 in 2024 with 67.4% support. Thompson and the International Order of Theodore Roosevelt (IOTR) are now working with lawmakers and advocates in states including Ohio, Colorado, Delaware and New Hampshire.

The point of those amendments is not to create a free-for-all or override wildlife regulations. States would still manage seasons, bag limits and conservation policy using science.

Instead, they create a higher legal threshold for activists seeking to eliminate hunting and fishing altogether.

"We know that anti-hunters are coming," Thompson said. "What we want is to ensure that when they get here, we’ve got a backstop."

IP28 is a perfect example of why that backstop could become important.

Four years ago, Thompson noted, many people dismissed an earlier version of the Oregon proposal because they didn't believe it would ever reach the ballot. It was too extreme. This year, the campaign came close enough to submit more than 142,000 signatures.

The fact that approximately 38,000 of those signatures were ultimately rejected is worth celebrating. But it would be foolish to assume the campaign is dead.

This was chief petitioner David Michelson’s third failed attempt to place the issue before Oregon voters. And he has made it clear that supporters view this as a long-term campaign, not a one-election project.

"We know that this is unlikely to pass in 2026," Michelson said in a previous interview. "No one on the campaign thinks that this will pass right now."

Instead, Michelson said the goal was to create an organization capable of pursuing similar initiatives in Oregon "in multiple election cycles in a row" and eventually launching them in other states.

Getting it onto the ballot would have helped IP28 supporters to collect voter data, build a donor base, normalize the proposal and identify language capable of attracting broader support next time.

That is unquestionably good news for Oregon’s hunters, anglers, farmers, ranchers, wildlife professionals and consumers.

But they also got close — much closer than during previous attempts.

Fly fishing for rainbow trout along the greenbelt in downtown Boise, Idaho. (Getty Images)

So enjoy the win, but keep paying attention.

Because IP28 will not be on the ballot this November, but the larger effort to eliminate hunting and fishing rights is not going anywhere. And neither can the people determined to protect them.

Love all things hunting, fishing and outdoors? Follow OutKick Outdoors on Instagram and TikTok!

title: Trump critic Massie joins Democrats in unprecedented bid to sue White House over Iran war
excerpt:
Brent Sadler, a former Pentagon official, addresses a report on the U.S.'s declining munitions stockpiles, a critical issue for potential major combat operations against Iran.

A lone House Republican...
body_text:
Brent Sadler, a former Pentagon official, addresses a report on the U.S.'s declining munitions stockpiles, a critical issue for potential major combat operations against Iran.

A lone House Republican is joining Democrats in an effort to get President Donald Trump sued over the Iran war.

Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., is one of the co-sponsors of a new resolution aimed at compelling House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., to sue the Trump administration over allegations the president is violating federal law with the U.S. conflict in the Middle East.

The bill is also being led by Rep. Gregory Meeks, D-N.Y., the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, as well as Reps. Jim McGovern, D-Mass., Gabe Amo, D-R.I., Pramila Jayapal, D-Wash., Jason Crow, D-Colo., and Ro Khanna, D-Calif.

Massie accused Trump and Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth of being "in blatant violation of two sections of the War Powers Resolution of 1973."

TRUMP AIMS TO RESET WAR POWERS CLOCK WITH CONTROVERSIAL BID TO BYPASS CONGRESS

Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., is part of a new push to fight back against President Donald Trump's war in Iran. (Win McNamee/Getty Images; Nathan Posner/Anadolu via Getty Images)

"For the first time since the law was enacted, a concurrent resolution has passed in accordance with 5(c) of the law, but the White House has ignored it. It seems they’ve assumed the law is unconstitutional, but no court has ever found that to be the case, so the law remains on the books while the White House flouts it. In the 1983 case INS v. Chadha, the Supreme Court did not opine on the 1973 War Powers Resolution. It’s time for the courts to settle this, and that’s what our legislation directs," Massie said.

"They’ve also violated section 5(b) of the law, but rather than ignore the law, they’ve perpetuated a ruse that the 60-day limit on Presidential military activity does not apply with respect to the Iran war, because each time they effect a temporary ceasefire, the statutory clock restarts. We believe no court would agree with this absurdity, and this should be litigated as well."

TRUMP-BACKED CANDIDATE ED GALLREIN CALLS KENTUCKY WIN A ‘DAVID VS. GOLIATH’ VICTORY AFTER DEFEATING MASSIE

Massie was one of four House Republicans who voted with Democrats to rebuke Trump over the Iran war with a war powers resolution that passed last week. The resolution is largely symbolic, however, and has no practical effect.

Rep. Gregory Meeks, D-N.Y., during a roundtable discussion with the House Foreign Affairs Committee on Feb. 12, 2025, in Washington, D.C. (Kayla Bartkowski/Getty Images)

His open criticism of Trump also earned Massie a primary challenger backed by the president, who wound up defeating the sitting congressman and will likely take his place in the House of Representatives next year.

But the new resolution to sue Trump over the Iran war is not likely to get a full House vote unless Massie or Democrats use maneuvers to force it over the objections of House GOP leaders.

REP TOM BARRETT: IT’S UP TO CONGRESS TO PREVENT ANOTHER ENDLESS AMERICAN WAR

In his comments to Fox News Digital, Massie also criticized congressional leadership for not doing more to block the war.

"Unfortunately, Speaker Johnson has chosen to let the power of our institution atrophy and is doing harm to our constitutional authority by his inaction motivated by political expediency," Massie said. "Although both Iraq wars and the war in Afghanistan were authorized by AUMFs [Use of Military Force] from Congress, the Trump administration has sought no such Congressional authorization for the war in Iran, and is therefore operating unconstitutionally."

Johnson, for his part, told reporters last week that he did not believe an AUMF was necessary but suggested he wanted to see an end to the war.

"The administration is working very hard. The commander in chief and the whole Department of War, they're working very hard to bring this to a resolution. There's a lot of discussions about how that will be done," Johnson told reporters Tuesday. "We're all closely watching those developments. Of course, I don't think an AUMF is in order right now. I think we need to bring this to a resolution."

Fox News Digital reached out to the White House for comment.

Elizabeth Elkind is a politics reporter for Fox News Digital leading coverage of the House of Representatives. Previous digital bylines seen at Daily Mail and CBS News.

Follow on Twitter at @liz_elkind and send tips to elizabeth.elkind@fox.com

Israeli raid sparks fire at UN Palestinian refugee centre

Israeli forces raided a United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees training centre in occupied East Jerusalem. Staff were detained, tear gas and stun grenades were fired, and a fire broke out. The raid follows warnings Israel planned to demolish the facility.

title: Slain TikTok influencer's ex begged for years to leave husband she outed as accused pedophile
excerpt:
A wealthy restaurateur is accused of killing his pregnant wife and their two children in a Texas murder-suicide. (KRIV)

TikTok influencer Sara Gilson's boyfriend had pleaded with her to cut ties with...
body_text:
A wealthy restaurateur is accused of killing his pregnant wife and their two children in a Texas murder-suicide. (KRIV)

TikTok influencer Sara Gilson's boyfriend had pleaded with her to cut ties with her estranged husband before authorities say he killed her.

Gilson, also known as Sara Duffey, made a post several weeks ago alleging her husband was a pedophile. Police in Owasso, Oklahoma, responded to a report of a domestic violence incident and found both Sara Duffey and Jeremiah Shawn Duffey dead, according to KTUL. The incident is being investigated as a murder-suicide.

A child inside the house called 911 and told the dispatcher "his step-father had shot his mother."

TIKTOK INFLUENCER WHO ACCUSED ESTRANGED HUSBAND OF PEDOPHILIA FOUND DEAD IN POSSIBLE MURDER-SUICIDE

TikTok influencer Sara Gilson, also known as Sara Duffey, left, was found dead alongside her estranged husband Jeremiah Shawn Duffey, right, in what Owasso, Oklahoma, police are investigating as a murder-suicide. (TikTok/@mrsgilson and @duffdaddy1)

Prior to being found dead, Sara Duffey made a TikTok on July 11 that was captioned, "Preparing for when Netflix drops a documentary about my soon to be ex husband who I just found out is a pedophile."

Lyle Landers, Sara Duffey's ex-husband, told People he had "begged" her to leave him.

NEW JERSEY NURSE GUNNED DOWN AT WORK BY ESTRANGED HUSBAND IN MURDER-SUICIDE: POLICE

"She had been stuck in a relationship where domestic abuse seemed ‘OK’ " Landers said. "I had begged her for five years to get away from him. I had offered to help her, in any way I could, to get away from him. But he seemed to have some sort of control over her, and she couldn’t seem to get away."

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

Gilson posted a TikTok video, following the format of a popular trend, in which she alleged her estranged husband was a "pedophile." (TikTok/ @mrsgilson)

"She was a wonderful mother and would die for her children. In fact, her trying to protect children is what ultimately led to her death," Landers said.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

On June 9, Owasso Police received a report from a parent and child accusing Jeremiah Shawn Duffey, a basketball coach, of touching a female child during an event held inside a school.

Police said similar accusations against Duffey had been reported before. He was accused of lewd molestations of a minor, with the case being sent to the U.S. Attorney’s Office.

Gilson had recently filed a protective order against Duffey and posted a video accusing him of sexual misconduct involving a minor. (TikTok/ @mrsgilson)

After the alleged incident, Sara Duffey filed an emergency protective order that barred him from the home.

That same day, another woman filed a separate protective order against Duffey, alleging he had been spotted "kissing and fondling" her 15-year-old daughter, a player on the youth basketball team he coached, according to The Oklahoman.

The outlet reported that he gave her money "to keep her quiet."

Adam Sabes is a reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to Adam.Sabes@fox.com and on Twitter @asabes10.

title: NY assemblyman calls for DOJ to investigate Mamdani, protect Jewish New Yorkers after stabbing attacks
excerpt: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu sharply criticizes New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, accusing him of ‘fomenting hate’ and creating fear among Jewish Americans in New York City, after Mamda...
body_text:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu sharply criticizes New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, accusing him of ‘fomenting hate’ and creating fear among Jewish Americans in New York City, after Mamdani called Netanyahu a ‘war criminal’ and threatened to arrest him.

A New York State assemblyman called on the U.S. Department of Justice to open a civil rights investigation into New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani following a pair of stabbings on Manhattan’s Upper West Side that are being looked at as potential hate crimes.

New York State Assemblyman Michael Novakhov, who represents District 45 in Brooklyn, called for action during an End Jew Hatred rally in New York City on Sunday.

"If the DOJ stepped in to protect Jewish students at Columbia, it must now step in to protect Jewish New Yorkers," Novakhov wrote in a post on Instagram with video of the announcement, referencing a federal probe into alleged antisemitism at the university.

SUSPECT ARRESTED AFTER ALLEGEDLY YELLING ‘ALLAHU AKBAR,' STABBING 2 MEN IN NYC ATTACK

Pro-Israeli protesters attend a rally in opposition to New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani in New York, Sunday, July 26, 2026. (AP Photo/Ryan Murphy)

Novakhov said he was sending the DOJ a formal letter requesting an investigation into New York State, New York City "and most importantly to investigate Mamdani’s hatred against the Jewish population of New York City and New York State."

Fox News Digital reached out to Mamdani’s office for comment but did not immediately hear back.

Pro-Israeli protesters hold signs at a rally in opposition to New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani in New York, Sunday, July 26, 2026. (AP Photo/Ryan Murphy)

The victims in Thursday’s stabbing attacks were identified in media reports as Chok Sung, 57, and Moshe Grunhaus, 50.

New York Attorney General Letitia James said both victims are currently in stable condition. The suspect, identified as Raul Morales, 51, is accused of yelling "Allahu Akbar" while stabbing two men on Thursday afternoon, according to officials.

The Upper West Side is known as a neighborhood with a large Jewish population, and Thursday was Tisha B'Av, a day when Jews fast in mourning for the destruction of the First and Second Temples in Jerusalem.

MAMDANI'S LATEST NETANYAHU REMARKS DEEPEN CONCERNS AMONG JEWISH LEADERS

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani speaks during a primary-night watch party for congressional candidate Claire Valdez at 99 Scott Studio on June 23, 2026 in Brooklyn. (Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)

"Jewish New Yorkers should not have to hide their Stars of David, tuck away their kippahs, or fear walking their own streets," Novakhov wrote.

"The Jewish community deserves answers. No one is above the law," his post read.

Jewish leaders have recently spoken out against Mamdani’s comments on Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, calling Netanyahu "a war criminal" and "the architect of a horrific genocide against the Palestinian people." Mamdani had added that while City Hall lacks the authority to arrest Netanyahu, he believes the prime minister should be held accountable under the International Criminal Court's warrant. This, despite the ICC not having any jurisdiction in the United States, as the U.S. is not a member of the international body.

Fox News Digital’s Greg Norman-Diamond and Rachel Wolf contributed to this report.

title: Scalise warns 'Bolshevik revolution' taking over Dem Party after socialist primary wins
excerpt:
House Majority Leader Steve Scalise spoke with Fox News Digital about the upcoming midterm elections.

The No. 2 leader in the House of Representatives is hammering Democrats after a slate of far-left...
body_text:
House Majority Leader Steve Scalise spoke with Fox News Digital about the upcoming midterm elections.

The No. 2 leader in the House of Representatives is hammering Democrats after a slate of far-left primary victories ahead of the November midterms, warning a "civil war" is in store for their party.

"There's like this Bolshevik revolution that has taken over the Democrat Party. It's scary to see because many of them are espousing communist viewpoints — very, very radical viewpoints — and they're winning. They're beating liberals," Scalise told Fox News Digital in an interview.

Republicans are seizing on wins by candidates affiliated with the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) as proof that Democrats as a whole are shifting further left than where most American voters are.

FAR-LEFT SURGE: MAMDANI-BACKED CANDIDATES OUST DEM ESTABLISHMENT INCUMBENTS

Then-New York Mayoral Candidate Zohran Mamdani, center, celebrates with Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., left, and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., right, during an election rally on Oct. 26, 2025, at Forest Hills Stadium in New York City. (Andres Kudacki/Getty Images)

"This is surely not your father's Democrat Party," Scalise said. "There's never been a sharper contrast between Republicans who believe in freedom and individual opportunity and Democrats who are moving toward socialism."

It comes after several DSA-linked candidates toppled incumbent progressive Democrats in recent weeks.

Reps. Adriano Espaillat, D-N.Y., and Dan Goldman, D-N.Y., both lost primaries to candidates backed by New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, himself a DSA member. Goldman's challenger Brad Lander, however, left the DSA after the Oct. 7, 2023, attack in Israel.

House Majority Leader Steve Scalise, left, and House Speaker Mike Johnson, during a news conference at the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C., on Nov. 5, 2025. (Daniel Heuer/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

MAMDANI-BACKED SOCIALIST WINS IN NEW YORK EXPOSE GROWING RIFT BETWEEN DEMOCRATIC ESTABLISHMENT, INSURGENT LEFT

Another DSA-backed candidate in Denver toppled longtime Rep. Diana DeGette, D-Colo.

Those victories in safe blue seats mean all three will have a glide path to the House of Representatives come November.

"The liberals in the Democrat Party are being beaten in primaries by socialists and that's foreboding for kind of this civil war that's going on in the Democrat Party," Scalise said. "I think if you go through most of middle America, and I go there a lot, all of those districts, they don't want socialism — and yet that's what's on the ballot."

Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee (DCCC) Chair Rep. Suzan DelBene, D-Wash., leader of House Democrats' campaign arm, told Fox News Digital in response that her party was focused on lowering costs and panned the GOP criticism as "desperate."

"The midterms will ultimately be a referendum on who is going to lower costs and help improve the lives of everyday Americans — which House Republicans have failed spectacularly to do. In the purple, majority-making districts — Democratic candidates are running substantive campaigns focused on lowering costs, saving health care, and fighting to make life affordable for working families," DelBene said. "Republicans already know they’ve lost the American people, and that’s why they are resorting to desperate attacks that aren’t actually about the pocketbook issues, but just baseless spin that falls flat with voters who are eager to reject Republicans."

Republicans are facing an uphill battle to keep control of the House in November, given historic trends that show the president's party traditionally faces significant losses halfway through the White House term.

But GOP leaders are hopeful that they can reverse that as lawmakers get ready to spend the entire month of August in their home districts making their case to Americans.

Elizabeth Elkind is a politics reporter for Fox News Digital leading coverage of the House of Representatives. Previous digital bylines seen at Daily Mail and CBS News.

Follow on Twitter at @liz_elkind and send tips to elizabeth.elkind@fox.com

title: Waltz slams France after stunning social media attack on US after UN vote
excerpt: Ambassador Jeff Bartos accused the U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights of condemning democracies while failing to confront abuses by authoritarian regimes, declaring that he had guided the U.N. hu...
body_text:
Ambassador Jeff Bartos accused the U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights of condemning democracies while failing to confront abuses by authoritarian regimes, declaring that he had guided the U.N. human rights system "to its deathbed." (UNTV)

France’s mission to the United Nations in Geneva launched a verbal attack against the U.S. following a contentious vote to give U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk another four-year term, accusing Washington of abandoning its role as a global human rights leader.

"The US used to be a beacon of human rights. Not anymore," the official French mission account posted on X Saturday. "Today, it stands alongside North Korea, Nicaragua, Mali & Russia, isolated. And the world no longer listens to it."

The mission added the hashtag "#AmericaAlone."

IRAN SECURES UN ROLE WITH BACKING FROM UK, FRANCE, CANADA, AUSTRALIA AS US STANDS ALONE

High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk speaks at a press conference at the UN Offices in Geneva on Dec. 9, 2022.  (Fabrice Coffrini/AFP via Getty Images)

U.S. Ambassador to the U.N. Mike Waltz fired back, accusing France of using the attack to distract from its support for Türk.

"It is disappointing — though not surprising — that this is how France deflects on its shameful vote to coddle some of the worst human rights abusers," Waltz wrote on X. "France voted for someone who has been lecturing free, sovereign democracies like the United States, the UK, and Israel, while cozying up to the world’s worst oppressors."

During the vote by Ambassador Jeff Bartos, the U.S. representative for U.N. management and reform, declared that the U.N. human rights system "has been losing credibility for decades."

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION TOUTS MORE THAN $1B IN UN BUDGET CUTS AS REFORM PUSH GAINS MOMENTUM

Ambassador Michael Waltz testifies during a House Foreign Affairs hearing on the United Nations in the Rayburn House Office Building on July 22, 2026. (CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)

"Mr. Türk has guided it to its deathbed," Bartos said. "And if you vote to reappoint Volker Türk for a four-year term, it will kick the bucket."

Bartos accused Türk of disproportionately condemning democracies while failing to respond adequately to abuses committed by authoritarian governments.

He said Türk had criticized the United States, Britain, France, Australia, Italy and, more than any other country, Israel. Bartos also accused Türk of remaining silent for 12 days after the Iranian government allegedly began a new wave of violence against its citizens, while quickly condemning U.S. military action against Iran.

Bartos further criticized Türk’s office for calling on Washington to lift sanctions on Cuba, maintaining what he called a discriminatory database targeting American companies and enabling the U.N.’s "anti-Israel machinery."

ISRAEL ACCUSES UN OF PLACING IT ON SAME SEXUAL VIOLENCE BLACKLIST AS HAMAS TERRORISTS, SEVERS TIES

U.N. Human Rights Council President Jurg Lauber, Secretary-General Antonio Guterres and High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk stand for a minute of silence honoring victims of human rights violations, at the opening of the 58th session of the United Nations Human Rights Council in Geneva, on Feb. 24, 2025. (Fabrice Coffrini/AFP via Getty Images)

France’s U.N. Ambassador Jérôme Bonnafont offered a sharply different assessment during the General Assembly debate, saying Türk had demonstrated "rigor and impartiality" during a first term marked by growing attacks on multilateral institutions and the universality of human rights.

"He has been a voice of conscience, confronting states with reality and their responsibilities," Bonnafont said.

An official familiar with the U.S. position told Fox News Digital on background that American officials were surprised by France’s "brazen" public attack and rejected the suggestion that opposing one U.N. official’s reappointment amounted to opposing human rights.

The official said Washington and other delegations were also caught off guard by the expedited vote because Türk’s current term does not expire until Oct. 11.

The United States sought to postpone consideration for one week to allow additional consultations, but member states rejected the request. The General Assembly then approved Türk’s reappointment by a vote of 144-10, with 13 abstentions, extending his tenure from Oct. 12, 2026, through Oct. 11, 2030.

The assembly also rejected a Russian proposal to extend Türk’s term only through the end of 2026, which would have allowed the next U.N. secretary-general to participate in selecting the human rights chief.

WORLD COURT PROSECUTOR WHO WENT AFTER NETANYAHU FOR WAR CRIMES SUSPENDED OVER SEXUAL MISCONDUCT

France's Foreign Affairs Minister Jean-Noel Barrot, right, greets Secretary of State Marco Rubio at the G7 Foreign Ministers' meeting in Cernay-la-Ville outside Paris, France, Friday, March 27, 2026. (Michel Euler/AP Photo)

France’s post grouped Washington with authoritarian governments that also opposed Türk, but did not address whether those countries voted against his reappointment for the same reasons. The U.S. said its opposition reflected both concerns about Türk’s record and objections to the accelerated process.

UN Watch, a Geneva-based watchdog, published a 2024 analysis of public statements initiated by Türk or his office between Oct. 17, 2022, and Oct. 31, 2024.

The organization concluded that Türk criticized the United States more frequently than China, North Korea, Cuba, Saudi Arabia and Qatar combined. It also said it found no self-initiated criticism during that period concerning abuses by Cuba, North Korea, Algeria, Eritrea, Mauritania, Lebanon or Qatar.

UN Watch’s methodology excluded statements required by the Human Rights Council, comments in mandated reports, broad updates to the council and other remarks that were not initiated at Türk’s discretion. Its findings therefore do not encompass every country reference, report or action by Türk’s office.

UN Watch Executive Director Hillel Neuer called the renewal "rushed and unprecedented" and said it was "unseemly" for French President Emmanuel Macron’s government to attack the United States while celebrating Türk’s reappointment.

Nile Gardiner, director of the Margaret Thatcher Center for Freedom at the Heritage Foundation, responded more bluntly.

"Perhaps show some gratitude instead?" Gardiner wrote on X. "The French owe their very existence as a sovereign nation to The United States."

FrenchPresident Emmanuel Macron and President Donald Trump. (Win McNamee/Getty Images)

Türk’s supporters argue that his willingness to criticize powerful democracies is part of his responsibility to apply human rights standards universally. France and the European Union maintained that he had performed his duties objectively and that Secretary-General António Guterres acted within the rules allowing a high commissioner to serve a second four-year term.

Türk is set to become the first U.N. human rights chief to serve two complete four-year terms since the position was established in 1993.

Efrat (Effie) Lachter is an investigative journalist, filmmaker and war correspondent. She has directed and produced over 200 documentary segments across more than 40 countries. Recipient of the 2022 Peres Center for Peace Award, Lachter is also a 2023-24 Knight-Wallace Journalism Fellow at the University of Michigan. She holds a bachelor's degree in communication and a master's degree in political science.

title: Montana man hikes 10 miles to safety after falling on trekking pole
excerpt:
David Cifaldi slipped and his pole pierced him in the side, then walked back hours along the route he had climbed

A Montana man walked 10 miles to safety with a trekking pole speared through his tors...
body_text:
David Cifaldi slipped and his pole pierced him in the side, then walked back hours along the route he had climbed

A Montana man walked 10 miles to safety with a trekking pole speared through his torso after a fall during a hiking expedition on the state’s highest mountain.

David Cifaldi slipped on rocks close to the summit of the 12,803ft (3,902 meters) Granite Peak during the hike on 20 July with two friends. He fell on one of his two poles, and “by the time I rolled over, I kind of knew something wasn’t right”, he told CBS news affiliate KVTQ.

The pole had pierced him in the side below his left arm, pushed out through his lower back, and only narrowly missed vital organs.

“Through my skin, I could feel the trekking pole,” he said. “I knew it wasn’t deep, and I knew I could take deep breaths.”

An emergency room nurse trained in wound care, Cifaldi said his medical background took over, and he and his friends made the decision to hike for six and a half hours along the route they had climbed, after alerting authorities using a satellite communicator.

“I think my nurse brain clicked on,” he said in a separate interview with Montana’s Local 12 news station.

“As soon as I was able to self-assess and establish that this was not life-threatening right now, I was pretty convinced I was going to get off that mountain under my own power.”

Cifaldi was taken to a local clinic after reaching the trailhead – then driven two hours by his friends to a hospital in Billings, where surgeons carefully removed the pole.

“I feel very lucky,” he said. “A couple inches the other way and this would be a different story.”

Cifaldi and his friends, Jesse Ross and Brad Reich, had set off at 3.30am to climb the mountain, which he said was a long-held ambition. They were about 1,000ft from the summit when the accident happened.

One of the friends walked behind Cifaldi to make sure he was steady on the rugged terrain back down while the other walked ahead to warn oncoming hikers.

“There’s families, and he … had us hike ahead and warn people so young kids didn’t have to see such a gnarly wound,” Ross told KVTQ. “Just so selfless.”

Ross expanded on the episode in an online fundraiser to pay for Cifaldi’s medical bills – and a new hiking vest.

“He self-assessed calmly: no bleeding, full feeling, no lightheadedness, nothing vital hit, and the pole stable in place,” he wrote.

“Given his condition, he made the call to self-rescue rather than wait for extraction – hiking 10 miles back to the trailhead with a trekking pole still through his body. [He] reached the trailhead entirely under his own power – never once complaining, staying in remarkably high spirits.”

When fully healed, Cifaldi said, the friends plan to attempt to reach the summit again.

Granite Peak’s peak is recorded in various places as between 12,799ft and 13,807ft. It was conquered in 1923, and only 17 climbers are known to have made it to the summit between then and 1953.

The mountain in the Beartooth range was the site of one of climbing’s greatest mysteries: the disappearance of Ernest Bruffey, 38, during a solo expedition in August 1959, the day an earthquake killed 28 people in Montana.

Human remains and a weathered boot believed to belong to Bruffey were found in 2000 by a group of six friends, one of whom had researched his disappearance.

title: Senate to begin voting on Trump intelligence nominee Jay Clayton – US politics live
excerpt:
The US president’s pick to be the country’s director of national intelligence is expected to be approved within days – but only after a tense confirmation hearing

Hello and welcome to the US politics...
body_text:
The US president’s pick to be the country’s director of national intelligence is expected to be approved within days – but only after a tense confirmation hearing

Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.

The Senate is due to begin voting as early as Monday on the nomination of Manhattan US attorney Jay Clayton, Donald Trump’s pick to be the ⁠top US spy, and he ⁠is expected to ​be approved within days despite a tense confirmation hearing.

If approved to be the director of national intelligence, Clayton would fill a role vacated in June when Tulsi Gabbard stepped down after ⁠a tenure marked by clashes with congressional Democrats, who accused her of advancing Trump’s political agenda and promoting debunked election claims.

The Senate is due to hold a procedural vote Monday evening on whether to advance ⁠Clayton’s nomination for the job overseeing the nation’s 18 intelligence agencies, Reuters reported.

The position of DNI was created after the 11 September 2001 attacks to ​coordinate the country’s sprawling intelligence apparatus.

Many senators are ‌eager for Clayton to take up ‌the post because they are unhappy with the interim director of national intelligence, Federal Housing Finance Agency director Bill Pulte, a Trump loyalist ‌without national security experience who has been cutting staff at the agency.

If Clayton wins a majority in the 100-member Senate on the procedural vote, a final confirmation vote is expected later in the week.

Trump’s Republicans, who have a 53-47 majority in the chamber and rarely break from the White House, are expected to provide Clayton with enough votes for confirmation.

The Pentagon updated its official war casualty database over the weekend, adding more than 140 wounded service members. The Defense Casualty Analysis System (DCAS) also introduced a new casualty category labeled “Overseas Operations” for personnel killed and wounded “starting July 7”. According to the updated database, the official toll for the earlier phase of the US-Iran war, known as Operation Epic Fury, now stands at 14 service members killed and more than 400 wounded in action.

Donald Trump’s Republican party has “nothing to run on” for the congressional midterm elections after the president broke promises to lower costs and avoid starting war overseas, Hakeem Jeffries has said. The House minority leader, a New York congressman, made those comments on CNN’s State of the Union on Sunday, exactly 100 days from the 3 November midterms, when Jeffries and his fellow Democrats are aiming to take control of the US House and Senate from their Republican opponents.

Benjamin Netanyahu said on Sunday that Zohran Mamdani, the New York City mayor, is “fomenting hate” by calling the Israeli prime minister a war criminal who should be arrested over Israel’s war in Gaza if he visits the city for the United Nations general assembly.

Tom Homan, the Trump administration “border czar”, on Sunday said he did not believe the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer at the center of a recent fatal shooting in Maine “should have ever cleared vetting”. Speaking to CNN’s State of the Union, Homan was asked by host Dana Bash about the officer’s eligibility to serve following reports that two of his ex-wives had accused him of abuse.

Pop star Katy Perry has condemned the Trump White House after it used her hit song Firework in a TikTok video showing US military strikes on Iranian targets, saying she never approved the use of her music. The White House video, which featured Firework playing over footage of a missile striking an Iranian naval ship, has amassed more than 6 million views. The post was captioned: “Iran has been warned.”

New Jersey governor Mikie Sherrill recently signed a new law prohibiting businesses from using shoppers’ personal information to charge different prices for identical products, making her state the third in the US to ban the practice. The Fair Price Protection Act passed by New Jersey’s legislature seeks to protect consumers from surveillance pricing, in which retailers can use data including online activity, location and purchasing history to arbitrarily change prices for individual shoppers.

President Donald Trump will visit General Motors at the Milford Proving Ground in suburban Detroit on Monday afternoon in defense of new, sweeping tariffs on Canada and his economic agenda ahead of primary contests next week.

Trump argues that tax cuts and tariffs protected 170,000 jobs in Michigan, crediting tariffs as the catalyst. “The President pledged to put Michigan workers back to work, and he’s doing it,” White House spokesperson Liz Huston said in a statement.

Michigan Democrats counter that the state’s residents have had to pay more than $2bn more for gasoline since Trump took office.

Trump announced a new round of tariffs on Canada on 20 July. The 50 percent tariff on imports ranging from wine to hockey sticks to cement begins in late August.

The Gordie Howe Bridge between Detroit and Windsor, Canada also opens today. It is unclear if Trump will visit the bridge, which has become another lightning rod for conflict between the US and Canada. A ribbon-cutting ceremony in Windsor was a Canada-only event after rescinding invitations following the tariff announcement.

Trump supported the bridge project during his first term, but has attacked it since retaking office, claiming that the terms of the bridge agreement are being renegotiated. “We changed the terms of the Deal so that the United States of America now gets 50% of the Profit,” Trump wrote on Truth Social.

What that actually means in practice is unclear. Canada paid for the bridge construction.

Democratic Senate hopeful Abdul El-Sayed likened the potential defeat of his opponents in the coming Michigan primary and November election to a stark exercise in progressive messaging, according to Politico’s Playbook.

“You’re gonna spend $60 million to beat me – OK, two can play at that game,” he said on a Zoom call with donors, Politico reported. “And then what happens is, ideally, you put one ogre on a pike, and then everyone else gets the message, and all of a sudden starts to sound a lot different.”

El-Sayed, a Rhodes Scholar, physician and former public health official in Michigan, faces US Rep Haley Stevens in 4 August primary for the US Senate, a seat Democrats almost certainly must hold to take control of the chamber in 2027. Retiring two-term Democratic senator Gary Peters currently holds the swing-state seat.

The contest pits El-Sayed, a progressive who has called for abolishing ICE and is aggressively opposed to US policy on Israel, against a relative moderate who last week voted against a bill amendment to end American financial support for Israel. The American Israel Public Affairs Committee has spent nearly $30m in the Michigan Democratic primary in support of Stevens.

El-Sayed described the contest in biblical terms.

“What they don’t really realize is that in spending so much money, they’re turning me into David, right?,” El-Sayed said. “So, like, if I’m the guy who came through and beat Goliath, now all of a sudden you just gave me the best platform in the entire US Senate, which I love because then guess where all eyes are going to be?”

Former US representative Mike Rogers is the presumptive Republican nominee.

The White House released an AI-generated video on Sunday night on the social media platform X, depicting President Donald Trump as Rick Sanchez from the Cartoon Network series Rick and Morty. In the video, Trump as Rick is running around the grounds of the White House, with what appears to be Vice-President JD Vance depicted as his grandson Morty. The video makes a reference to Trump taking a third term in office, which the president joked about at the White House Correspondent’s Dinner on Friday night. 
  The video has, at this moment, 6.3 million views on X.

President Donald Trump plans to tout his handling of the economy during a visit to suburban Detroit today, defending sweeping tariffs in a swing state where their effects have hurt many businesses as midterm election season heats up.

Trump is visiting a General Motors facility in Milford, home to tracks and proving grounds for new models and vehicles. Early voting is underway for Michigan’s 4 August primary, which features fierce nomination fights in both major political parties, AP reported.

Republican Mike Rogers is unopposed in the Senate primary, but the GOP gubernatorial contest pits Trump-backed John James against Perry Johnson, a businessman turned politician who has launched unsuccessful campaigns before, including for president in 2024.

Johnson is now trying to style himself in the president’s mold - despite missing out on his endorsement.

The House minority leader, a New York congressman, made those comments on CNN’s State of the Union on Sunday, exactly 100 days from the 3 November midterms, when Jeffries and his fellow Democrats are aiming to take control of the US House and Senate from their Republican opponents.

Asked to discuss the elections, Jeffries alluded to how Trump and other Republicans quickly seized on a 21 July announcement from Mike Sherrill, the Democratic New Jersey governor, that 6,600 noncitizens in the state had registered to vote because of a software error.

Fewer than 400 of them voted before the identification and correction of the error. But the president and his allies nonetheless used the disclosure to boost false claims that there are scores of noncitizens on voter rolls who could compromise the integrity of the midterms, during which Republicans are predicted to lose seats.

Jeffries on Sunday argued that was because it is a more comfortable strategy to adopt rather than confront how the US and Israeli militaries began warring with Iran in February after Trump won a second presidency in 2024 having promised “not to start … endless wars in the Middle East”.

The costs of the war have included the deaths of 18 US troop members as of Sunday, along with injuries to hundreds more. Gas and grocery prices have also soared amid the conflict, leaving 95% of Americans believing that the US is suffering an affordability crisis, according to exclusive polling conducted for the Guardian.

Let's get the f...

Darby Fox, a licensed clinical social worker, joined 'Fox & Friends First' to discuss the rise in violence at youth sporting events and the parents' role in kids' athletic activities.

Let's get the final Monday of July 2026 rolling with a fresh edition of Monday Screencaps where we cook up some content before football season gets cranked up. Guys, I'm disappearing for a few days after this column to get some family vacation time in before the kids dive into school sports and the school year starts in two weeks.

It's that time of the year. It's now or never for those final family getaways, which means SeanJo will be with you the rest of the week.

IDAHO TEEN UMPIRE DELIVERS ULTIMATE REALITY CHECK TO COACH COMPLAINING ABOUT WALK-UP MUSIC

TONY ROMO'S BRUTAL GOLF SCORE BEFORE GETTING ARRESTED PAINTS A NIGHTMARISH PICTURE

Jang Won-young throws out the ceremonial first pitch before the game between the Los Angeles Dodgers and the New York Mets at Citi Field on Sunday, July 26, 2026, in New York, N.Y. (MLB Photos via Getty Images)

Imagine going out in public looking like this. And we're supposed to listen to what this woman has to say about America from her living room in Ireland?

– Jeff E. emails: If you took all the soccer I’d watched in my life and compared it to FIFA in US it’s not even close.  Maybe watched four or five games - even watched some that were not USMT. Here's the top and bottom three list for soccer:

-Red Card (often over prescriptive - someone should tell them how hockey does it)

-Time keeping (added time, lack of precision, lack of communication to those watching)

-Flopping, the worst thing about soccer (many had taken LeBron James master class)

– Marty in Idaho always sends in cool content: Some readers are having squirrel problems in their back yard. I get that squirrels can be annoying but let’s add some perspective. In late June a buck deer died in the tall grass in my back yard from an antler injury we think. Not much I could do so I just put a game camera on it to see what happened. Mountain lions (mama and three cubs) found it within the hour and spent most of the next two nights feeding on it. If you watch the video, our house is about 75 yards to the left. I let the neighbors know so nobody would go out for a moonlight stroll.

– Loyal reader Ricky A. is spending his summer in Japan:

– Robert R. on how to get to Wisconsin while avoiding Chicago: I lived in FL 35 years and moved to TN in 2019.  I'm from WI originally, my oldest lives near Green Bay and since 1997 I have been making the trip to visit at least once a year .  I solved the Chicago problem about 10 years ago.  I now leave I 57 and head west to Bloomington about 40 miles before Chicago, use I 72.

At Bloomington head north to Rockford and then at Janesville you can take 43 to Milwaukee or go to Madison and use 51 north to Fond du Lac.  Adds about an hour or a little more but: less traffic, only 1 toll (at Rockford) for about $2 .  I hate going through Chicago, my daughter in-law used to call and ask where I was and my response was always "the 7th ring of Hell".

– John in Milford, MI advises me to take up smoking: It will take commitment on your part, but I have a solution to your problem with your neighbor’s cigarette smoke that I guarantee will work. I smoked long ago when I was young, and I can tell you that the urge to run out and pick up a carton of Winstons never goes away. I still find the smell of cigarette smoke enchanting. All you need to do is start smoking yourself, huff a pack a day for a few years, then quit cold turkey.  I promise that you will look forward to being downwind from your neighbor and catching a whiff of tobacco smoke after that. Problem solved.

– Jim in East Peoria, IL has a simple solution: LEAF BLOWER!!! Hell yes!!! Dumbass me should have thought of that. And a real f–king loud and big and annoying one would be in order methinks.

Also, those Miami girls are definitely going to give the Dallas team a run for their money!!!

Kinsey: I did have my leaf blower next to me on the patio Saturday afternoon. I'll have to try this next time the neighbor lights up the cigs.

This went down over the weekend in Madison, WI. Very simple solution. Pepper spray water cannons. Clear the whole area. If they want to come back. Blast them again. Clear the way for red-blooded Americans who want to suck down a beer or whiskey on a Saturday night while maybe chasing some skirts.

That is it this morning. SeanJo will have you until Saturday morning when I will be back. Send him emails. Send him your deep thoughts. And keep Respecting Summer while I'm out.
