title: CNN panelist blames 'culture war' retribution as reason for Ryan Clark's ESPN departure
excerpt:
Dan Dakich reacts to Jemele Hill attempting to rip OutKick following the outlet receiving sourcing during the Ryan Clark layoff.

Ryan Clark is no longer employed by ESPN.

After it was first reported...
body_text:
Dan Dakich reacts to Jemele Hill attempting to rip OutKick following the outlet receiving sourcing during the Ryan Clark layoff.

Ryan Clark is no longer employed by ESPN.

After it was first reported by OutKick that Clark would be among a collection of on-air talents let go by the four-letter network Tuesday, July 21, the story shifted focus to a combination of cause and blame around the situation, and not the termination itself.

Clark was told the news on Monday during a taping of ESPN's 'NFL Live' after OutKick had obtained the information and had asked the network for comment. ESPN acted in such a manner, telling Clark during a taping, in an attempt to keep OutKick's Dan Zaksheske and Bobby Burack from breaking the story.

SPORTS MEDIA RUSHES TO CAST RYAN CLARK AS VICTIM WHILE PORTRAYING ESPN AS THE VILLAIN

Ryan Clark was let go by ESPN after more than 11 years with the network, OutKick learned. (Ric Tapia/Getty Images)

In his first public comments following his ouster, Clark accused ESPN of intentionally leaking the news to OutKick. The fact that OutKick obtained the information hasn't exactly sat right with at least one CNN contributor.

During 'CNN This Morning' on Sunday, Jason "Jah" Lee raised questions about the situation as a whole while also pointing to Clark getting caught up in a "culture war" leading to his demise at ESPN.

ESPN parted ways with longtime NFL analyst Ryan Clark following an 11-year run at the network. (Michael Allio/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

OUTKICK IS NOW ON THE FOX APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

"I think Ryan Clark got swept up in some level of culture war retribution," Lee, the senior editor at Bossip, explained. "The reason he got fired during the segment is because an outlet called OutKick contacted ESPN threatening to leak this information. How would OutKick get this information?

"OutKick is owned by Fox News Corp and was established by Clay Travis. If you know Clay Travis, he is not a bleeding-heart liberal. I feel a lot of this was purposefully done to embarrass Ryan Clark. ESPN has taken a lot of heat for being a liberal bastion lately, and I feel like perhaps [Clark's] bosses thought this was a time to push the other direction."

Ryan Clark, who joined ESPN after retiring from the NFL in 2015, was let go by the network. (Patrick McDermott/Getty Images)

Clark, a former Super Bowl champion with the Pittsburgh Steelers, began his NFL analyst career at ESPN in 2015. According to Burack, he made around $2 million per year, roughly four times what the average NFL analyst earns.

title: TikTok influencer who accused estranged husband of pedophilia found dead in possible murder-suicide
excerpt:
A wealthy restaurateur is accused of killing his pregnant wife and their two children in a Texas murder-suicide. (KRIV)

TikTok influencer Sara Gilson, also known as Sara Duffey, posted weeks ago alle...
body_text:
A wealthy restaurateur is accused of killing his pregnant wife and their two children in a Texas murder-suicide. (KRIV)

TikTok influencer Sara Gilson, also known as Sara Duffey, posted weeks ago alleging that her husband was a pedophile. The estranged couple has since been found shot to death in the woman's Oklahoma home in what is reportedly believed to have been a murder-suicide.

Gilson, who had recently filed a protective order against her husband, 48-year-old Jeremiah "Shawn" Duffey, posted the TikTok video on July 11. It was captioned, "Preparing for when Netflix drops a documentary about my soon to be ex husband who I just found out is a pedophile." The video was still visible on her account as of Saturday.

Gilson had recently filed a protective order against Duffey and posted a video accusing him of sexual misconduct involving a minor. (TikTok/ @mrsgilson)

Thirteen days after she posted that video, police reportedly responded to a domestic call on July 24 at 41-year-old Gilson's home. When officers arrived, they found Gilson and Duffey dead from apparent gunshot wounds, according to local outlet KTUL.

FORMER DEM VIRGINIA LT. GOV. KILLS WIFE, HIMSELF IN SHOCKING MURDER-SUICIDE: POLICE

KTUL cited an extended family member who identified the pair as the dead bodies in the home and said that Jeremiah, who went by Shawn, allegedly broke into the home, killed Sara and then himself. Police confirmed the couple's identities, according to local outlet KRMG, but did not say if it was a murder-suicide.

Police insisted there was no threat to the public at this time, according to KRMG.

HOUSTON RESTAURATEUR SUSPECTED OF KILLING PREGNANT WIFE AND TWO CHILDREN BEFORE TAKING HIS OWN LIFE

Police found Sara Gilson and Jeremiah "Shawn" Duffey dead after responding to a domestic call at her home, according to local reports. (TikTok/ @mrsgilson; Ajax9, iStock via Getty Images)

Authorities also said that the 911 call came from a juvenile in the house, the local media outlets reported.

Duffey had been ordered to stay at least 100 yards away from Gilson as part of her June 10 protective order against him.

On the same day she filed her protective order, another woman filed for a separate protective order against Duffey after he was allegedly spotted "kissing and fondling" her 15-year-old daughter, who played on the youth basketball team Duffey coached, according to The Oklahoman.

TEACHER WHO SERVED AS GOP STATE LAWMAKER ALLEGEDLY USED ROBLOX TO LURE STUDENT INTO SEXUAL RELATIONSHIP

Duffey had allegedly been sending the girl inappropriate messages and had given her money "to keep her quiet," the outlet reported.

After the coach was allegedly spotted with the girl, a report had been filed to the Owasso Police Department.

Gilson posted a TikTok video, following the format of a popular trend, in which she alleged her estranged husband was a "pedophile." (TikTok/ @mrsgilson)

Gilson had also filed two previous protective orders against Duffey, though both were dismissed after Gilson failed to appear at the hearings, People reported.

Gilson and Duffey had reportedly shared children of their own.

Fox News Digital contacted the Owasso Police Department for confirmation and further details.

title: Trump ‘border czar’ says ICE officer in Maine killing should not have cleared vetting
excerpt:
Tom Homan comments on officer’s eligibility to serve after reports that agent’s two ex-wives had accused him of abuse

Tom Homan, the Trump administration “border czar”, on Sunday said he did not beli...
body_text:
Tom Homan comments on officer’s eligibility to serve after reports that agent’s two ex-wives had accused him of abuse

Tom Homan, the Trump administration “border czar”, on Sunday said he did not believe the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer at the center of a recent fatal shooting in Maine “should have ever cleared vetting”.

Speaking to CNN’s State of the Union, Homan was asked by host Dana Bash about the officer’s eligibility to serve following reports that two of his ex-wives had accused him of abuse.

“Should someone with those issues be an ICE agent?” Bash asked.

“No, if those … are facts … I don’t think he should ever have cleared vetting,” Homan replied.

Homan also said part of an ongoing investigation into the 13 July shooting death Joan Sebastián Durán Guerrero is determining “how … did the vetting process fail”.

“When they hire somebody, they put them through a vetting process and look at all that stuff. So I know, based on that information – that’s part of the ongoing investigation,” Homan said. “How … did the vetting process fail? Was that information not available? Did they not know?”

He added: “So there’s a separate administrative investigation on what happened here. Did we have that information? Did we not have that information? But the vetting process … if that was factual, he would have an almost impossible time to pass vetting.”

The officer involved in the killing of Durán Guerrero, a 25-year-old Colombian man in Biddeford, Maine, has since been identified by news outlets as David Brouillette. The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS), which oversees ICE, has not publicly confirmed Brouillette’s identity.

Since the shooting, two of Brouillette’s ex-wives have publicly described alleged abuse during their relationships with him. One, Lucinda Brouillette, alleged her ex-husband engaged in a “persistent pattern of abuse, intimidation, manipulation, fear and control”.

“If you were to ask me whether I believe David Brouillette is capable of this level of violence, my answer is unequivocally yes,” she said in a statement to NPR.

Although Homan declined to comment directly on this particular case, describing it as “a rare instance”, he said: “If this person had that type of history, it would have been a vetting issue, and it should have been brought to the attention of those who make those decisions.”

He added, in part: “We will see. It’s all being reviewed. We will see where it lies.”

The shooting has prompted renewed scrutiny of ICE’s hiring practices.

Democrats have called for reviews of the agency’s vetting process. For instance, Mississippi congressman Bennie Thompson, the top Democrat on the US House homeland security committee, said that Brouillette’s alleged abusive past “directly call[s] into question the supposed vetting and training ICE does of its recruits”.

Neither the fatal shooting in Maine nor another one involving an ICE officer in Texas earlier in July yielded body camera footage from officers. That prompted Homan to announce that the agency would require officers to wear body cameras during vehicle stops.

In the Texas case, which resulted in the killing of Mexican national Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, the Harris county district attorney Sean Teare said in a statement that lab results of a white substance found in a van at the center of a case tested negative for narcotics or illicit drugs – despite an FBI search warrant application that maintained a bag with substance in question was consistent with methamphetamine.

Salgado’s family had said the substance was a salt mixture that he and his construction crew colleagues used as electrolytes to stay hydrated in extremely hot temperatures.

The Associated Press contributed reporting

title: This red state is strengthening its grip as America's next economic heavyweight
excerpt:
Gabriela von zur Muehlen, chief policy officer at the Texas Association of Business, says Texas’ low costs and strong supply chains help attract billionaires, CEOs and manufacturers.

The race to beco...
body_text:
Gabriela von zur Muehlen, chief policy officer at the Texas Association of Business, says Texas’ low costs and strong supply chains help attract billionaires, CEOs and manufacturers.

The race to become America's next economic heavyweight may already have a frontrunner.

The latest Internal Revenue Service (IRS) migration data show billions of dollars in taxpayer wealth flowing into Texas, while Census figures show the state's largest metropolitan areas continue to outpace much of the country in population growth, strengthening a decades-long shift in America's economic center of gravity.

What's more, Texas isn't relying on a single boomtown. Dallas-Fort Worth added more residents than any metropolitan area in the country over the past year, while Houston, Austin and San Antonio also ranked among the nation's fastest-growing metros.

That unusual breadth gives Texas multiple engines of economic growth, providing businesses with larger labor pools, diversified industries and a broader customer base than states anchored by a single dominant city.

Critics have argued that Texas' economic success is mostly a numbers game. But the latest federal data suggest there's more to it. (Mike Lawrie/WireImage/GettyImages)

BILLIONS IN TAXPAYER INCOME ARE LEAVING TWO ICONIC STATES — AS A NEW ECONOMIC MAP EMERGES

The population boom has been accompanied by an influx of wealth. IRS migration data analyzed by the Tax Foundation show the Lone Star State gained more than $5 billion in adjusted gross income from interstate movers, while California and New York recorded multibillion-dollar losses.

"Capital follows where there is confidence," Texas Association of Business Chief Policy Officer Gabriela von zur Muehlen previously told Fox News Digital. "And right now there is a tremendous amount of confidence in Texas."

Von zur Muehlen said Texas' tax structure and predictable regulatory environment continue to attract businesses and investment from other states, helping reinforce the state's economic momentum.

While Florida attracted the nation's largest influx of taxpayer wealth and South Carolina posted the strongest inbound migration rate, Texas stood out by combining billions in new taxable income with rapid growth across Dallas-Fort Worth, Houston, Austin and San Antonio.

Economists say that combination matters because higher-income households bring spending, investment, entrepreneurship and tax revenue that can accelerate job creation, fuel commercial development and attract even more businesses. Over time, those forces can transform fast-growing metros into some of the nation's most influential economic hubs.

ONE SOUTHERN CITY YOU'VE NEVER HEARD OF IS GROWING FASTER THAN ANYWHERE ELSE IN AMERICA

Unlike simple population counts, adjusted gross income offers a glimpse into the economic resources newcomers bring with them. Higher-income households can contribute disproportionately to consumer spending, investment and local tax collections, making income migration an important measure of a region's long-term economic strength.

The migration data are only part of the story.

Earlier federal estimates showed Texas wasn't just adding residents — it was becoming wealthier on a per-person basis. Despite adding roughly 419,000 residents in 2025, more than any other state, Texas' economic output climbed to about $2.9 trillion, while per-capita GDP continued to rise, suggesting the state's economy was becoming more productive rather than simply larger.

THE RED STATES RACING AHEAD IN AMERICA'S POWERFUL WEALTH BOOM — AND THE STATES FALLING BEHIND

As businesses leave high-cost states, Texas has become the undisputed top destination. (Tom Fox/The Dallas Morning News/Getty Images)

Business leaders say those trends are creating a self-reinforcing cycle. As more workers and higher-income households relocate to Texas, companies gain access to a larger labor pool and customer base, encouraging additional hiring, investment and expansion. That growth, in turn, creates more jobs and opportunities that can attract even more residents.

The migration has coincided with years of corporate relocations and business investment across the state, particularly in technology, finance, manufacturing and energy. The influx has also fueled new housing developments, logistics hubs, manufacturing projects and expanding commercial corridors across many of Texas' fastest-growing metropolitan areas.

Supporters of Texas' economic model argue its lack of a state income tax, relatively affordable cost of living and business-friendly climate continue attracting both employers and workers, reinforcing the state's long-term growth.

California and New York remain among the nation's largest and most influential economies.

But the latest Census, IRS and federal economic data suggest Texas continues gaining ground by attracting people, taxpayer wealth and economic output simultaneously, an uncommon combination that could reshape where businesses invest, jobs are created, and economic influence grows over the coming decade.

Amanda Macias covers the intersection of business, economics and politics, with a focus on how policy decisions shape markets, businesses and American workers.

title: Berlin police shoot dead suspect in car ramming attack on Pride event
excerpt:
German police have shot dead the suspect wanted in a car-ramming attack on Berlin’s Pride march.

Abdul Ballout, a German citizen with Lebanese roots, was killed on Sunday as he attacked officers with...
body_text:
German police have shot dead the suspect wanted in a car-ramming attack on Berlin’s Pride march.

Abdul Ballout, a German citizen with Lebanese roots, was killed on Sunday as he attacked officers with a bladed weapon, police said. Officials said all indications pointed to a “Islamic terror attack”.

Ballout was shot after a search that lasted nearly 24 hours. He was the main suspect in the attack that took place on Saturday evening in which a van drove into a crowd in central Berlin. The car ramming killed one person and injured 29.

The shooting occurred in the German capital’s Spandau district. Police said Ballout died despite efforts to resuscitate him.

“Around 6 p.m. (1600 GMT), the suspect involved in yesterday’s attack in Tiergarten was located at an allotment garden complex in Spandau,” Berlin police wrote on social media.

“According to initial findings, he ran towards officers while armed with a bladed weapon; police … subsequently opened fire. Despite immediate resuscitation efforts by the Berlin Fire Department, he died at the scene.”

title: Black bears invade Lake Tahoe homes as break-ins surge and locals fortify defenses
excerpt: A curious black bear pushed open the front door of a Southern California water district office, wandered inside to sniff around as stunned employees watched, then calmly let itself out and returned to...
body_text:
A curious black bear pushed open the front door of a Southern California water district office, wandered inside to sniff around as stunned employees watched, then calmly let itself out and returned to the woods. (Crestline Village Water District)

Black bears are increasingly breaking into homes around Lake Tahoe, leaving residents to spend thousands of dollars protecting their properties from hungry wildlife.

So far this year, South Lake Tahoe police have received 174 bear-related calls, compared with 97 during the same period last year, according to The Wall Street Journal. Several incidents involved bears making their way into homes.

One local couple told the publication they were washing dishes when they looked up to find a bear standing in their living room.

HIDDEN DANGER AT POPULAR US NATIONAL PARK FORCES TRAIL CLOSURES AS BEAR SIGHTINGS CLIMB

The animal wandered through the house, sniffed a tube of toothpaste in the bathroom and urinated on the floor before leaving. It was the couple's second bear break-in within the span of a month, the publication said.

As encounters become more common, some homeowners have begun installing electric mats, reinforced doors and other deterrents that can cost thousands of dollars.

Black bears are increasingly breaking into homes around Lake Tahoe, turning bear-proofing into a costly necessity for many homeowners. (iStock)

Resident Margaret Deanesly Ziegler has installed everything from electric deterrents to a steel door to protect her summer cabin from bears, spending about $7,500 in the process, WSJ reported.

"I heard the most god-awful noise," the retired physician told the publication. "I heard the house being wrenched, the wood being torn apart."

"The bears are winning," Ziegler said. "I'm the one that's spending the money."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Similar encounters have occurred across the Lake Tahoe Basin in recent weeks.

Fox News Digital previously reported that a California man deployed bear spray after a black bear charged toward him outside his vacation home over the Fourth of July holiday. He spotted the animal rummaging through a garbage can inside his garage.

Some homeowners have begun installing electric mats, reinforced doors and other deterrents that can cost thousands of dollars. (iStock)

Video of the encounter captured the bear rushing toward the homeowner before he deployed the spray, sending the animal running away.

The California Department of Fish and Wildlife notes on its website that black bears are "highly food-motivated" and naturally investigate attractive smells in search of food.

The department recommends eliminating food attractants and blocking access to them with bear-proof containers, electric fencing or electric mats. It also warns that bears accustomed to human food can become increasingly bold and destructive, while cubs often learn those behaviors from their mothers.

The increase in encounters has also sparked debate among Lake Tahoe residents over whether bears or people are driving the problem.

Officials recommend eliminating access to food attractants by using bear-proof containers, electric fencing or electric mats. (Joe Hendrickson/iStock)

"We don't have a bear problem, we have a people problem," one Reddit user wrote.

Another resident shared that a bear broke into their home earlier this year despite keeping trash secured, writing that they eventually installed bear mats because "it's just the price we pay to live side by side with bears."

Others said bears have remained a routine part of life around Lake Tahoe and that conflicts can often be avoided.

"Bears have been fine in my neighborhood," one user wrote. "Don't leave food or trash out and they just wander through."

Fox News Digital's Brittany Miller contributed to this report.

Kelly McGreal is a production assistant with the lifestyle team at Fox News Digital.

title: Israel launches military incursion into Syria amid UN condemnation
excerpt:
The head of the United Nations has condemned the persistent violation of Syria’s sovereignty, as Israel’s forces reportedly carried out new incursions into its neighbour’s territory.

Israeli soldiers...
body_text:
The head of the United Nations has condemned the persistent violation of Syria’s sovereignty, as Israel’s forces reportedly carried out new incursions into its neighbour’s territory.

Israeli soldiers advanced towards villages in southwestern Syria on Sunday, setting up a checkpoint at Al-Ardah, while shelling was also heard nearby, Syria’s state news agency SANA reported. Leaflets were dropped warning residents against attempting to obstruct the advance of Israeli vehicles.

The incursion came as United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, on a visit to Syria, condemned Israel’s violations.

“Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity & territorial integrity must be fully respected,” he wrote in a social media post. “Violations by Israel of the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement are unacceptable & must stop.”

Speaking at a press conference on Sunday, he said that the UN is set to submit a comprehensive report to the UN Security Council on the issue at the end of the month.

Israel has conducted increasingly regular incursions into Syrian territory since the fall of the regime of ousted President Bashar al-Assad in December 2024.

In the immediate aftermath, it seized control of the UN-controlled buffer zone separating the Israeli-occupied Golan Heights from the rest of Syria, saying the 1974 disengagement agreement with Syria had collapsed.

Since then, Israel has carried out regular attacks, raids and searches, and established military checkpoints further within Syria.

Israeli officials say they intend to remain in southern Syria, in what they call a “security zone”.

Syria’s Foreign Minister Asaad Hassan al-Shaibani called for Israel’s withdrawal from the buffer zone on Saturday, saying its continued military operations and occupation are a “direct threat to the security of the region”.

In an exclusive interview with Al Jazeera’s Al Muqabala, Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa said Damascus was working to reach a security agreement with Israel, involving a group of countries.

“If the security agreement with Israel succeeds, it will pave the way for comprehensive peace without conceding Syria’s right to the occupied Golan [Heights],” he said.

He said that Syria has “no interest” in entering a confrontation with Israel.

Guterres’s visit to Syria is the first by a UN chief to the country since 2009. He is expected to visit the UN Disengagement Observer Force (UNDOF), which has been deployed to the buffer zone since 1974.

On Sunday, he described the country as being at a “moment of opportunity” to recover from its 13-year war, and build a more stable, inclusive and prosperous future.

The UN chief urged the removal of all sanctions imposed on the country during the era of al-Assad, who was deposed by forces led by al-Sharaa in 2024 after over a decade of civil war.

“I welcome steps that have eased sanctions, and opening new possibilities for economic recovery, but all these sanctions must be removed immediately,” Guterres said.

Western countries including the United States have begun lifting economic sanctions, but investors remain cautious. The World Bank has estimated the country’s post-war reconstruction could cost $216bn.

“The United Nations stands with the people of Syria at this pivotal moment. And I came carrying the strongest possible appeal to the international community, an appeal to spare no effort to support the Syrian people and to support the Syrian government,” Guterres said.

title: Mamdani's politics linked to Muslim Brotherhood ideology as New York violence escalates: report
excerpt: Jessica Tarlov and Lizzy Savetsky join Bill Hemmer and Shannon Bream for a panel discussion on soaring antisemitism in New York City after two recent stabbings near Central Park. Rabbi Ari Berman, Pre...
body_text:
Jessica Tarlov and Lizzy Savetsky join Bill Hemmer and Shannon Bream for a panel discussion on soaring antisemitism in New York City after two recent stabbings near Central Park. Rabbi Ari Berman, President of Yeshiva University, criticizes Mayor Mamdani's "obsessive focus" on Israel, claiming it betrays New Yorkers. Lizzy Savetsky connects Mamdani's anti-Israel rhetoric to rising hate.

On Tisha B'Av, the saddest day in the Jewish calendar marking the destruction of the Temple in Jerusalem and the long history of catastrophes that followed, an assailant armed with a knife walked up to two men on Manhattan's Upper West Side and stabbed them. One wore a yarmulke.

Witnesses said the assailant shouted, "Allahu Akbar." The victims, ages 50 and 57, survived. A suspect is in custody, and police are examining the motive. But New York City did not need to wait for a formal designation to understand the gravity of the crime that had been perpetrated.

Only a day earlier, Zohran Mamdani, the mayor of the city with the largest Jewish community in the Diaspora, released a video accusing Israel of war crimes and genocide — and declared that Benjamin Netanyahu, the elected leader of the region's only democracy, should be arrested.

SUSPECT ARRESTED AFTER ALLEGEDLY YELLING ‘ALLAHU AKBAR,' STABBING 2 MEN IN NYC ATTACK

FILE - New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani recently admitted that he lacks the legal authority to arrest Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu after saying his office was looking into the potential action. (Fox News Digital/Deirdre Heavey)

The mayor of an American city has no such power. Municipal leaders are forbidden by law from carrying out their own foreign policy. Nevertheless, Mamdani’s public relations stunt, amplified not only on social media but by the media of record, used language decrying the Jewish state as a criminal enterprise and suggesting that its defenders are fair game, setting the stage for bloodshed.

Jewish organizations had warned that the climate in the city was becoming dangerous. Their prescient warnings became prophetic as police officers cleaned up the crime scene.

It would not be appropriate to claim that any politician placed the weapon in the hands of the man who allegedly stabbed two innocent New Yorkers while attempting to terrorize the American Jewish community.

JEWISH LEADERS FAULT MAMDANI RHETORIC AS UPPER WEST SIDE STABBING, HATE CRIME PROBE CONTINUES

I contend something far more uncomfortable and dangerous: words and ideas lead to such actions, and a public culture that brands the Jewish state as genocidal or apartheid and treats "resistance" as a virtue normalizes a permission structure — in the dockets of justice and in the halls of power — in which such violence becomes thinkable.

This is the argument of a report that the Institute for the Study of Global Antisemitism & Policy (ISGAP) published on Mamdani in 2025. It is the argument that the events of this week have tragically underscored.

The report traces the origins of Mamdani’s worldview. As a student at Bowdoin College, Mamdani co-founded a chapter of Students for Justice in Palestine. In the aftermath of Oct. 7 — the largest single-day massacre of Jews since the Holocaust — he downplayed the atrocity while characterizing Israel's legally justified defensive response as genocide.

A woman reacts as the community of Kibbutz Kfar Aza commemorates their members who were killed, taken hostage and died in captivity, following the deadly Oct. 7, 2023, attack by Hamas terrorists, in Kibbutz Kfar Aza, southern Israel, Oct. 16, 2025. (Hannah McKay/Reuters)

FAR-LEFT STREAMER HASAN PIKER DEFENDS HIMSELF FROM ANTISEMITISM ACCUSATIONS IN INTERVIEW WITH JEWISH OUTLET

He repeatedly declined to condemn the slogan "globalize the intifada," offering only that he would "discourage" its use, as though a call to export anti-Jewish violence to the streets of America were merely a matter of etiquette. He introduced legislation to punish New York charitable institutions that support Israel. His first act as mayor, before addressing police unions and garbage collection, was to remove the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance definition of antisemitism from the city’s lexicon.

He accepted a $100,000 donation from the Council on American-Islamic Relations, an organization identified by federal prosecutors as an unindicted co-conspirator in a terrorism-financing case, and he has associated with figures such as Imam Siraj Wahhaj, who served as a character witness for the man convicted of masterminding the 1993 World Trade Center bombing.

These are not stray data points. His close friend, influencer Hasan Piker, and political candidates Mamdani has openly endorsed assert that the United States deserved what it got on Sept. 11, 2001 — a travesty as we prepare to honor the 25th anniversary of the attack on New York City itself. Mamdani’s words and actions form a dangerous pattern, and that pattern has a name: the Muslim Brotherhood.

ISGAP research on the Brotherhood's strategic entryism into North America describes a century-long campaign that its own internal documents lay out plainly. "The Project" of 1982 and the "Explanatory Memorandum" of 1991 — evidence entered in federal court — describe a strategy the authors call "civilization jihad": to exploit the freedoms of Western democracies to hollow them out from within, patiently, over generations, until the host society no longer recognizes what has been done to it.

FILE - Twitch streamer Hasan Piker is facing renewed scrutiny after viewers spotted a framed newspaper front page from Sept. 12, 2001, in his background. (Sam Barnes/Web Summit via Sportsfile via Getty Images)

Front organizations advise governments, shape civil-rights policy, embed themselves in universities and cultivate media, all while presenting a moderate face. Qatar underwrites much of it. Students for Justice in Palestine and American Muslims for Palestine sit within this ecosystem, and Hamas, which calls itself the Palestinian branch of the Muslim Brotherhood and which the U.S. has designated a foreign terrorist organization, is what the ideology produces.

The Brotherhood is Sunni; the revolutionary regime in Tehran is Shia. On almost everything else, they are rivals, yet they converge on one project: the destruction of Israel and the humiliation of the West. When an American mayoral candidate adopts the same moral and political map, in which Israel is the aggressor and its enemies are the aggrieved, he is not dissenting bravely from consensus. He is translating a dangerous ideology into the fluent, sympathetic idiom of Western progressivism, where it does its most effective work precisely because it no longer seems foreign.

This is why the antisemitism at the center of Mamdani's politics cannot be waved away as a mere progressive ideology. Antisemitism is the oldest early-warning system a society has. It begins with Jews, and it never ends there. The same worldview that marks Jews as obstacles also marks pluralism, free exchange and the liberal democratic order itself as enemies. An assault on the Jews of New York is an assault on the idea of New York, on the essence of the American democratic experiment.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani later released a video admitting that he lacks the legal authority to arrest Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, though it did little to ease Jewish leaders' concerns. (NYC Mayor's Office via YouTube/Handout via Reuters)

Listen closely to how Mamdani talks about his own city. The wealthy, landlords and the "billionaire class," in his telling, are a shadowy few who hoard the city and lock everyone else out. The language is reminiscent of Der Sturmer and the films produced by Joseph Goebbels. Presented as economic justice, this is familiar and dangerous rhetoric.

The oldest antisemitic libels have always relied on the image of a rich, rootless minority pulling the strings while ordinary people suffer. When a politician's economic populism runs on the same rails as his hostility toward the Jewish state, the two are not unrelated. They draw from the same well. This is why the assault is not merely on Jews or Israel. It is on the very fabric of the U.S. — on the idea that a free society is built through commerce, contract, and pluralism rather than resentment, expropriation and the search for an enemy within.

A man was knifed outside a synagogue on the saddest day of the Jewish year in a city whose mayor spends his energy accusing the Jewish state of genocide. We must say clearly what connects the rhetoric to the risk, refuse the normalization of hatred dressed up as social justice, and insist that words that prepare the ground for violence be named for what they are before the next knife is drawn.

Unrestrained by his theatrical and ineffectual call for Netanyahu’s arrest, Mamdani now calls for massive demonstrations when the Israeli leader visits the city for the U.N. General Assembly in September.

FILE - New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani previously said his administration was exploring whether the city has legal authority to arrest Netanyahu if he visits for the U.N. General Assembly. (Ronen Zvulun/Pool/AFP via Getty Images)

"The mayor’s activist posturing puts police officers on the street in a terrible position," New York City Police Benevolent Association President Patrick Hendry said. "Protests during the U.N. General Assembly are nothing new, but when the mayor of the city is actively calling for demonstrations, violent agitators will assume they have permission to cause as much havoc as possible."

The stabbings in Manhattan are just the beginning of something far more dangerous. Mamdani, it appears, has sounded the call, content that the globalization of the intifada will erupt on the streets of the city he is sworn to serve.

Charles Asher Small is the founder and director of the Institute for the Study of Global Antisemitism and Policy.

title: Christopher Sanchez's dominant home ERA makes Phillies run line the play against Yankees
excerpt:
Kyle Schwarber hit his second home run to extend the Phillies' lead over the Cubs.

It was a bit of a dull weekend on the diamond. I haven't been all that impressed with the matchups. Usually, basebal...
body_text:
Kyle Schwarber hit his second home run to extend the Phillies' lead over the Cubs.

It was a bit of a dull weekend on the diamond. I haven't been all that impressed with the matchups. Usually, baseball has some really good pairings for the weekend, but now and then, there aren't too many impressive series. I do like the Seattle and Texas one, but we've covered them once, and I don't have a great read on the game today. So, I'm going with the other game that I like - New York vs. Philadelphia.

The New York Yankees are just two games back in their division, but for whatever reason, it feels like this team is on the verge of a collapse. Maybe I'm exaggerating here, but something about the conversation from the media is that the Yankees are falling apart. I don't quite see it, but they do have a very talented roster on the injured list, so maybe that's the issue. The good news for them is that Ben Rice is having a fantastic season, their players could all return healthy in plenty of time, and they are still a likely playoff team.

New York Yankees' Ben Rice high-fives teammates after scoring a run during the third inning against the Athletics in West Sacramento, Calif., on May 31, 2026. (Scott Marshall/AP)

The Yankees are looking for a sweep today, and they send out Will Warren to get the job done. Warren has been fine this year. He has been reliable, tossed a reasonable number of innings, and hasn't missed any time due to injury. He did, for some reason, pitch for less than an inning in relief on Wednesday. His numbers are seven wins and four losses, with a 4.00 ERA and a 1.37 WHIP. Philadelphia hitters have seen him 31 times and gotten eight hits, with only Kyle Schwarber launching one over the fence.

AARON JUDGE OFFICIALLY OUT INDEFINITELY WITH STRESS FRACTURE IN HUGE BLOW TO YANKEES' TITLE HOPES

The Philadelphia Phillies have been one of the better teams in baseball this season. They are 5.5 games back of the Braves at the moment, but this was a division that looked like Atlanta would lock up by the end of May, so this has been some progress. Looking at the team and players' statistics, the one thing that has stood out to me is that Schwarber leads them in homers, Brandon Marsh leads in average, and Bryce Harper leads in RBIs. It isn't just that three different guys lead them in three different categories; it is that there are even more on the team having really strong years. They have six guys hitting .240 or better.

Philadelphia Phillies' Kyle Schwarber celebrates his home run with Bryce Harper during the third inning against the New York Mets in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania on June 20, 2026. (Chris Szagola/AP)

It shouldn't be surprising that a good team has players performing well. Part of what makes the Phillies so dangerous is their ability to not need just one guy to carry the load. In the rotation, I will say one guy, tonight's starter, does seem to be carrying his weight and then some. Christopher Sanchez is having another solid year with a 12-4 record, 2.64 ERA, and a 1.19 WHIP. Sanchez has been fantastic at home with a 1.03 ERA as well. Honestly, the only bad home start he has had was the All-Star Game. Yankees hitters are hitting just .200 against him in 45 at-bats.

I'm sure we can find a player prop if you're looking for that sort of thing. Ever since sports betting became legal basically everywhere, I feel like the daily fantasy stuff is not as popular. Maybe it is, and I'm just not paying attention. Either way, Cody Bellinger is someone you might want to add on the team, and Ryan McMahon is someone to fade.

Philadelphia Phillies pitcher Christopher Sanchez (61) delivers a pitch against the New York Mets during the first inning at Citi Field. (Gregory Fisher-USA TODAY Sports)

For the game, there are two options here - the Phillies, despite losing the first two games of this series, should win tonight. Sanchez has been great in Philadelphia. Paying -193 for them to win is not something I'm interested in. Instead, I am going to take the Phillies on the Run Line tonight. I've made this point before and need to follow it more. The Yankees have had 25 1-run games this year, and the Phillies have had 27. In 105 games, that's less than 25% of their final scores being decided by a run. Give me the Phillies -1.5.

title: Everyday Revolutionary War heroes take center stage in Trump's 'Spirit of '76' exhibit
excerpt: Fox News Digital gets an exclusive guided tour of the 'Spirit of '76' exhibit with designer Matthew Taylor, who shares the stories of some overlooked Revolutionary War heroes and Caesar Rodney's legen...
body_text:
Fox News Digital gets an exclusive guided tour of the 'Spirit of '76' exhibit with designer Matthew Taylor, who shares the stories of some overlooked Revolutionary War heroes and Caesar Rodney's legendary midnight ride.

EXCLUSIVE: Beneath a towering 23-foot bronze figure holding the Declaration of Independence aloft, designer Matthew Taylor stopped beside an equestrian statue that many Americans have likely never seen, or even heard of.

"Most Americans have never heard of Caesar Rodney," Taylor told Fox News Digital during an exclusive tour of the new Spirit of '76 exhibition at Freedom Plaza. "But we owe this man an enormous debt of gratitude."

The temporary installation, unveiled as part of America's 250th anniversary celebration, transforms Freedom Plaza into an open-air gallery honoring Revolutionary War figures whose names rarely appear in history textbooks.

Commissioned by President Donald Trump, the exhibition features 22 statues and sculptural installations, including a restored equestrian monument of Rodney, a towering "Spirit of Liberty" centerpiece, bronze figures representing Revolutionary soldiers, and an immersive memorial honoring Americans who died aboard British prison ships during the Revolution.

EXPERTS FINALLY SOLVE MYSTERY OF TEENAGE REVOLUTIONARY WAR SOLDIER 246 YEARS AFTER HIS DEATH

Matthew Taylor stands beneath the Caesar Rodney statue with members of the fabrication team during the opening of the Spirit of '76 exhibition at Freedom Plaza. (Dan Fleuette)

According to the National Park Service, the exhibit was created to honor the "heroes and martyrs of the Revolution" during America's semiquincentennial and is intended to celebrate the enduring "Spirit of '76' that continues to live on in every American heart."

The centerpiece installations include the Caesar Rodney equestrian statue, the "12 Soldiers of the Revolution," the Prison Ship Martyrs memorial and the 23-foot Spirit of Liberty statue.

ARCHAEOLOGICAL DIG AT BATTLE OF BUNKER HILL SITE UNCOVERS REVOLUTIONARY WAR ARTIFACTS

The restored Caesar Rodney equestrian statue stands at Freedom Plaza during the opening of the Spirit of '76 exhibition in Washington, D.C. (Dan Fleuette)

Rather than beginning with George Washington or Thomas Jefferson, however, Taylor chose to introduce visitors to Rodney.

The Delaware statesman, one of the signers of the Declaration of Independence, is remembered for his legendary overnight ride from Dover to Philadelphia in July 1776. Suffering from severe illness, Rodney rode roughly 80 miles through a storm to cast the vote that broke Delaware's deadlock in favor of independence.

"Of all the signers of the Declaration of Independence, Caesar Rodney is one of the most exciting," Taylor said. "When Delaware's delegation was deadlocked, he rode through the night to cast the vote that helped secure American independence."

THE REVOLUTIONARY LANDMARKS WHERE WASHINGTON, ADAMS AND JEFFERSON CHANGED AMERICA

A welder from Atelier Missor places final touches on the "Spirit of Liberty" statue before the installation was made public earlier this month. (Dan Fleuette)

For decades, the bronze statue stood in Wilmington's Rodney Square before being removed in 2020. It now occupies one of the most prominent locations in the nation's capital, just blocks from both the White House and the Capitol.

From Rodney's ride, Taylor naturally guides visitors into the next chapter of the American story.

Arranged around the plaza are bronze sculptures representing 12 Revolutionary War soldiers. Rather than depicting famous generals, the statues celebrate ordinary Americans whose individual stories reflect the sacrifices of the Revolutionary generation.

"These are ordinary citizens who did extraordinary things," Taylor said. "Every one of these statues tells the story of someone who answered the call during the Revolution."

An inscription featuring a quote from George Washington appears on the base of the Spirit of Liberty statue at Freedom Plaza in Washington, D.C., during America's 250th anniversary celebration. (Dan Fleuette)

Among them is Samuel Whittemore, who fought British troops at age 78. According to Taylor, Whittemore was bayoneted multiple times, shot in the head and left for dead before surviving and living into his 90s.

Another figure, Simon Knowles, enlisted at just 15 years old and served alongside George Washington throughout much of the Revolutionary War before returning home to live as a farmer.

Taylor said those stories represent the exhibition's central message.

"Unlike monuments to George Washington or Thomas Jefferson, these statues honor ordinary Americans who did extraordinary things," he said.

Nearby, another installation tells one of the Revolution's lesser-known tragedies.

Designed as visitors physically walk through its narrow bronze panels, the Prison Ship Martyrs memorial recreates the outline of a British prison ship. According to the National Park Service, nearly 12,000 Americans died aboard prison ships during the Revolutionary War; even more than were killed in combat during the conflict.

Taylor said the memorial is meant to immerse visitors in that experience.

"As you walk inside, you hear the water from the fountain," he explained during the tour. "It helps place you inside the story."

The fountain itself has also become part of the experience. Taylor noted it was recently restored to operation after years of sitting idle, providing the soundscape surrounding the memorial while complementing the plaza's redesign.

The Prison Ship Martyrs memorial at Freedom Plaza honors Americans who died aboard British prison ships during the Revolutionary War. (Dan Fleuette)

Towering above the entire exhibition stands the Spirit of Liberty, a new bronze figure inspired by iconic American monuments while looking toward the country's next 250 years.

Standing 23 feet tall, the statue holds an exact bronze replica of the Declaration of Independence in one hand while raising a sword skyward with the other. Around its base are reliefs depicting three defining moments of the Revolution: the signing of the Declaration of Independence, George Washington crossing the Delaware River and the British surrender at Yorktown.

"The Spirit of Liberty represents the sacrifices that gave birth to this nation," Taylor said.

During Fox News Digital's visit, visitors gathered around the plaza to photograph the statues against the Washington skyline. Low-angle views of the bronze figures framed them against bright summer skies, while Rodney's horse appeared frozen mid-stride as though continuing the historic ride that helped shape the nation's founding.

For Taylor, whose career has largely been spent both behind the camera and behind the scenes designing historical works, the exhibition is about more than commemorating famous names.

Instead, he hopes visitors leave thinking about people they had never encountered before arriving at Freedom Plaza.

"When visitors leave here," Taylor said, "I hope they realize they can do extraordinary things themselves. America was built by ordinary citizens who answered extraordinary moments."

The Spirit of '76 exhibition is free to the public and is scheduled to remain on display throughout the nation's 250th anniversary celebration.

Jasmine Baehr is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital, where she covers politics, the military, legal debates surrounding life and family policy, as well as faith and culture.

title: Industry star David Jonsson to play Black Panther in Marvel sequel
excerpt:
Director Ryan Coogler announces British actor in lead role alongside co-stars Letitia Wright and Winston Duke

The British actor David Jonsson has been unveiled as the new Black Panther by the film’s ...
body_text:
Director Ryan Coogler announces British actor in lead role alongside co-stars Letitia Wright and Winston Duke

The British actor David Jonsson has been unveiled as the new Black Panther by the film’s director, Ryan Coogler.

Jonsson, 32, known for roles in Industry, The Long Walk and Alien: Romulus, will play the son of Chadwick Boseman’s T’Challa in the third Black Panther movie.

He joined Coogler on stage at Marvel Studios’ Comic-Con International presentation to announce the news on Saturday, alongside co-stars Letitia Wright and Winston Duke.

Coogler, who won the Oscar for best original screenplay for his vampire film Sinners earlier this year, said: “The last time we got to make a movie, we introduced a character who is the son of the character that the great Chadwick Boseman played – our T’Challa – in that film.

“And today, I want to tell you that in this next film, he grows up, he comes of age.”

Born in London, Jonsson began his career in the West End. He made his screen debut in 2018 in two episodes of the British detective drama Endeavour before being cast as Augustus “Gus” Sackey in the first two series of Industry from 2020 to 2022.

He appeared in the 2025 adaptation of Stephen King’s thriller The Long Walk and in the same year won the Bafta rising star award.

Jonsson, who also has roles in the upcoming films The Chaperones, Benn/Eubank and Scandalous, said: “Thank you to this family that I have the honour and the blessing to join. I don’t want to say too much, because I want to let the screen do the talking.”

Black Panther III will be released in US cinemas on 15 December 2028. A UK release date yet to be confirmed.

Boseman died in 2020 aged 43, four years after being diagnosed with colon cancer.

Black Panther: Wakanda Forever, released in 2022, revealed that Boseman’s character, T’Challa, had a son. It followed Wright’s character, Shuri, as she takes on the role of the protagonist after the death of T’Challa.

The first film, released in 2018, was set in the mythical country of Wakanda, a hidden African kingdom with innovative technology thanks to its reserves of the world’s most useful precious metal. It won three Oscars.

Coogler, who directed the first two Black Panther movies, also co-produced the 2025 series Ironheart and Eyes of Wakanda.

title: Katy Perry ‘deeply appalled’ over White House using her song in Iran war video
excerpt:
Singer rebukes Trump administration after it uses her song Firework over footage of missile striking Iranian naval ship

Pop star Katy Perry has condemned the Trump White House after it used her hit s...
body_text:
Singer rebukes Trump administration after it uses her song Firework over footage of missile striking Iranian naval ship

Pop star Katy Perry has condemned the Trump White House after it used her hit song Firework in a TikTok video showing US military strikes on Iranian targets, saying she never approved the use of her music.

The White House video, which featured Firework playing over footage of a missile striking an Iranian naval ship, has amassed more than 6 million views. The post was captioned: “Iran has been warned.”

Perry responded on Saturday with a statement on X criticizing what she called the unauthorized use of the song.

“I am deeply appalled and angry to see ‘Firework’ used on the White House TikTok account as a backing track for video footage of military strikes,” the singer said. “I did not approve this, I was not asked, and I absolutely do not condone it.”

Perry continued: “I wrote this song to be an anthem of hope, healing, and inner strength for people going through their darkest personal moments. To see a message of self-worth and upliftment weaponized to soundtrack destruction and violence is a complete violation of everything my song stands for. My music is for bringing people together, not celebrating warfare.”

The White House launched its TikTok account in August 2025, when Donald Trump threatened to ban the platform months into his second presidency.

Perry is among a number of artists to criticize the Trump administration over the unauthorized use of music in government social media posts, with the president picking fights with several – mostly female – pop singers.

Olivia Rodrigo previously criticized the administration after one of her songs appeared in a government video promoting deportation efforts.

Beyoncé also blocked Trump from using her song Freedom after it was featured in a campaign video on social media. The track had served as the central campaign song for former vice-president Kamala Harris, who lost the 2024 White House election to Trump.

In March, Kesha condemned the White House’s use of her song Blow in a military-promotional TikTok video, calling it a “show of blatant disregard for human life”.

Sabrina Carpenter spoke out after her hit song Juno was used in a Trump-posted video showing Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers making arrests. Carpenter called the video “evil and disgusting” and told the administration: “Do not ever involve me or my music to benefit your inhumane agenda.”

In June, Ariana Grande also rebuked the White House for using her song Bye in a social media post promoting US immigration arrests, describing the video as “barbaric”.

Singer Jess Glynne also objected after the White House used her song Hold My Hand in a post on X promoting ICE deportations. Glynne said she felt “sick” that her music was being used to spread “division and hate”.

It was revealed in December that Perry is in a relationship with former Canadian prime minister Justin Trudeau, who is familiar himself with Trump’s trolling. He has repeatedly been targeted by Trump, who has continuously threatened to impose tariffs on Canada and has even suggested the US should annex the country, referring to Trudeau as the “governor” of the “Great State of Canada”.

The Defense Casualty Analysis System (DCAS) lists the official death toll for the US-Iran conflict at 14 service members, with 420 total personnel wounded in action.

Those official metrics, however, have been subject to ongoing controversy due to a sudden drop from the 18 deaths and 482 wounded recorded days earlier.

The collapse of the ceasefire with Iran and the subsequent resumption of near-daily airstrikes starting on 6 July have sparked debate over how casualties are counted. Analysts and officials have questioned whether victims from the two weeks since should be tracked in a separate tally, a move that would be unprecedented.

The Trump administration is attempting to have the latest resumed strikes in Iran be treated as a separate campaign from Operation Epic Fury, the US military’s official name for the Iran conflict. The separate casualty count beginning 7 July stems from that.

The US House member Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican, responded to the updated numbers in an X post, writing, “Let me explain this absurd ruse: The Pentagon is pretending there have been two Iran wars separated by a brief cease-fire.

“The reality: By going more than 90 days without congressional authorization,” the defense secretary, Pete Hegseth, “IS BREAKING THE LAW and must be held accountable”.

title: Los Angeles Rams betting outlook: why one analyst is all in on a Super Bowl win at +550
excerpt:
Los Angeles Rams HC Sean McVay joins Colin Cowherd to discuss the Rams drafting Alabama QB Ty Simpson 13th overall, coaching reigning MVP Matthew Stafford, and being the Rams HC for his 10th season.

...
body_text:
Los Angeles Rams HC Sean McVay joins Colin Cowherd to discuss the Rams drafting Alabama QB Ty Simpson 13th overall, coaching reigning MVP Matthew Stafford, and being the Rams HC for his 10th season.

If you watched the Super Bowl last year, you were probably a bit disappointed. I’m sure you weren’t if you were a Seahawks fan, and I know that I was happy about some of the outcomes, but the game itself was a bit boring. That was a lot different than the NFC Championship game, which was a fantastic back-and-forth battle between the Seahawks and the team we break down here, the Rams.

As mentioned, the Los Angeles Rams made it to the NFC Championship before falling short against the Seahawks. It was a good run, but the Rams did look vulnerable in each of their playoff games. They started against the Panthers and seemed like they were going to lose until they had some Matthew Stafford heroics. Speaking of Stafford, he ended up with one of the best seasons of his career and the MVP award. In the Divisional Playoffs, he capitalized on a bad route or bad throw (depending on who you ask) from the Bears and stole a 20-17 overtime win. He was great against the Seahawks, but the Rams defense couldn’t get a stop.

REIGNING MVP MATTHEW STAFFORD LOCKS IN EXTENSION WITH RAMS WORTH UP TO $60M WITH INCENTIVES

Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford leaves the field after the 2026 NFC Championship Game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field in Seattle, Wash., on Jan. 25, 2026. (Steven Bisig/Imagn Images)

That inability to get a stop may be part of the reason that Los Angeles went out and made a major splash this offseason. They traded for Myles Garrett, arguably the best defensive player on the planet at the moment. It was so big that even Aaron Donald is considering coming back to the team, and out of retirement. Stafford is coming back after contemplating retirement, so they shored up that concern. They added Trent McDuffie, one of the better cornerbacks in the league, and grabbed Jaylen Watson from free agency to address the other side of their secondary. Their defense should be even better.

Myles Garrett of the Los Angeles Rams poses with his jersey during a press conference after an organized team activities workout at Rams Village at the Warner Center in Woodland Hills, California, on June 2, 2026. (Kevin Terrell/Getty Images)

If Donald comes out of retirement, he probably won’t be quite as elite as he was in the past, but I have to imagine he is still in shape and would be ready by the time the season starts. It doesn’t look like he is coming, though. Still, this defense, which was solid but not great last season, could be amazing this season. I don’t know that Stafford will lead the league in touchdowns and yards, but he still has Davante Adams and Puka Nacua. If his offensive line protects him and gives him time, he will carve up even the best defenses he faces.

Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay reacts as players warm up before the NFC Championship NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks, Sunday, Jan. 25, 2026, in Seattle. (AP Photo/Stephen Brashear)

I am all in on the Rams this year. I think they are the best team in the NFL and have very few exploitable weaknesses. They are in a tough division – the Seahawks will still be good, the 49ers are always a tough team – but I think 11.5 wins is an over for them. I have them at 13 wins for the year. I also like them to win the Super Bowl at +550. Maybe I’m overconfident in their defense with Garrett or a 38-year-old quarterback, but I think the Rams have all the pieces and will close the deal this season.

title: England’s north-south life expectancy gap grows despite record longevity
excerpt:
King’s Fund report finds men and women live, on average, for 80 years and nearly 84 years, but gains are in south

The north-south divide in life expectancy in England has grown over the past decade, ...
body_text:
King’s Fund report finds men and women live, on average, for 80 years and nearly 84 years, but gains are in south

The north-south divide in life expectancy in England has grown over the past decade, with people in northern regions facing more illnesses such as heart disease and cancer, but also suicides and deaths related to alcohol and drug misuse.

Provisional figures show life expectancy reached an all-time high in 2025, with men and women in England living, on average, for 80 years and nearly 84 years respectively, but the gains were overwhelmingly in the south, the King’s Fund said.

Despite suffering the sharpest fall in lifespan during the Covid pandemic, life expectancy in London rose by nearly a year in the decade to 2023-25. The south-east, south-west and east of England also recorded gains.

But the half of England’s population who live in five northern regions, namely the north-west, the north-east, Yorkshire and the Humber, West Midlands and East Midlands, experienced little or no rise in life expectancy over the same period, reflecting greater levels of deprivation.

According to the health charity, people in London can now expect to live three years longer than those in the north-east. Even starker disparities emerged at the local level, with life expectancy in Blackpool, Lancashire, being 10 years shorter for men and eight years shorter for women than in Hart, Hampshire.

“In the most deprived 30% of areas, life expectancy either fell or didn’t improve over the past decade and that’s a disturbing story,” said Veena Raleigh, a senior fellow at the King’s Fund. “Meanwhile, it went up by half a year in the least deprived 30% of areas.”

“Over the past decade, the north has fallen further behind, and the plans for levelling up and the regeneration of the north haven’t materialised,” Raleigh added. “This isn’t just a question of fixing the health service. It requires a cross-government drive to also address the wider, underlying determinants of health, for example, ensuring people have secure jobs, fair pay, adequate housing, clean air, accessible transport and affordable access to healthy diets.”

The government’s 10-year plan for the NHS aims to increase healthy life expectancy – the number of years people spend in good health – for everyone in England, while halving the gap between the richest and poorest. But the King’s Fund called the goal “unrealistic”, requiring improvements in population health on a scale not seen in decades.

Healthy life expectancy fell in all regions of England in the decade to 2022-24, with people now spending on average about 2.5 years longer in poor health, the charity found. The regional divide has remained unchanged at about six to seven years, but can reach 20 years between the most and least deprived regions. The figures mean those in the most deprived parts of England have shorter lives and spend more years in poor health.

“Although the government’s 10-year health plan promises a shift from sickness to prevention, the focus is mainly on reducing waiting lists and waiting times,” Raleigh said. “Public health and prevention of ill health need to be much higher up the policy agenda, for example, to tackle the rising prevalence of obesity.

“The increasing prevalence of ill health in adults of working age, in particular, is deeply concerning because it risks jeopardising the life course of some young people with, additionally, the high costs of rising economic inactivity.”

A Department of Health and Social Care spokesperson said the government’s aim to halve the gap in healthy life expectancy reflected the “scale and complexity of the challenge”. They said £2.2bn was being repurposed for critical resources such as medicines and medical equipment in deprived areas.

“Someone’s postcode should never dictate how long they live, and this government is determined to tackle the stark inequalities that still exist across Britain,” the spokesperson said. “We’re already taking action, from allocating GP funding more fairly to delivering pioneering neighbourhood health centres in the areas that need them most. But we will now go further in devolving power to local communities, putting decision-making into the hands of those who know their areas best and driving lasting change across the country.”

title: Israel obstructing takeover of pilot zones in Lebanon’s south: Military
excerpt:
The Lebanese army has accused Israel of obstructing its efforts to take over control of security in southern Lebanon.

The Lebanese military said in a statement on Sunday that the Israeli army was con...
body_text:
The Lebanese army has accused Israel of obstructing its efforts to take over control of security in southern Lebanon.

The Lebanese military said in a statement on Sunday that the Israeli army was continuing to conduct shelling and clearance operations, preventing Lebanese troops from fully taking over villages as agreed.

The Lebanese army on Tuesday deployed troops to the first of three “pilot zone” villages. The move for local forces to take over security follows the signing last month of a United States-backed agreement that should see the phased withdrawal of the Israeli army from southern Lebanon.

“The continuation of these assaults hinders the completion of the army’s deployment … and prevents the return of residents to their villages and towns,” the Lebanese army said in its statement.

Three villages, or “pilot zones”, were chosen for the first phase of the Israeli withdrawals – Zawtar al-Gharbiya, Froun and Srifa. However, concerns over the lack of a clear exit schedule from Israel have persisted.

Parts of western Zawtar, Tibnit and Nabatieh al-Fawqa were still seeing Israeli gunfire even as civilians returned home, the Lebanese military said on Sunday.

Israel was bulldozing, shelling and conducting combing operations with machine guns in Nabatieh, Hdda, Kunin, Bint Jbeil, Nabi Ibel al-Saqi, Khiam, al-Mansouri and Bayt al-Siyad as well as Majdal Zoun in Tyre, it added.

A water project in the town of Markaba was also blown up while olive trees and swathes of farmland were razed on the outskirts of the town of Aitaroun.

Reporting from Zawtar al-Gharbiya, Al Jazeera’s Zeina Khodr said displaced residents had returned to homes of rubble.

The Israeli army had withdrawn to the edge of the village but was conditioning further movement on the dismantling of Hezbollah, she said.

Israel has occupied locations across southern Lebanon for months, insisting its presence is necessary to fight Hezbollah.

The Iran-backed armed group has rejected the US-brokered deal, demanding Israel’s unconditional exit.

Lebanese President Joseph Aoun visited US President Donald Trump in Washington, DC, last week in a bid to persuade him to pressure Israel into complying with their agreement.

Fighting erupted once again in Lebanon in March after Hezbollah fired rockets at Israel in response to the US-Israel war on Iran and their killing of Iranian Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei.

At least 4,330 people have been killed while 37 Israeli soldiers and four Israeli civilians have died in the latest round of violence.

title: Witness recounts Fourth of July weekend Bigfoot sighting in Connecticut, says 'there were no boobs'
excerpt: Todd Neiss, an American Primate Conservancy founder, shares his belief in Bigfoot after experiencing sightings in Ohio. Neiss discusses eerie howls and enormous footprints reported by locals, explaini...
body_text:
Todd Neiss, an American Primate Conservancy founder, shares his belief in Bigfoot after experiencing sightings in Ohio. Neiss discusses eerie howls and enormous footprints reported by locals, explaining that his own encounter during a military exercise in 1993 made him a believer. He describes the creatures as very large and athletic.

In the early morning hours of July 5, a man saw a Bigfoot shortly after leaving a cabin a friend of his had rented in Voluntown, Connecticut, presumably for the Fourth of July weekend. The man was making his way back home to Rhode Island at the time.

After leaving the cabin's long dirt driveway and crossing a bridge on the road, he wrote to The Bigfoot Field Researchers Organization that he "witnessed something jump into the road from my right heading to the woods on my left."

He had to hit his brakes so that he wouldn’t hit the "bipedal, 8-8½ foot tall creature." The presumed Bigfoot didn’t stop and never looked at him as it crossed the road in front of him.

A man says a Bigfoot walked in front of his vehicle after he left a cabin early in the morning during Fourth of July weekend. (Getty Images/iStockphoto)

TWO LADIES, A DOG, A LIGHTHOUSE AND A POSSIBLE BIGFOOT ENCOUNTER ON A BEACH IN MICHIGAN

"It had coarse, matted, and greasy looking long brown hair covering every part of its body I could see," wrote the witness who went on camera with an investigator a few days after the sighting.

"Its legs were shorter than its torso and its arms literally hung down to right around knee height. Must have had an 8 - 9ft 'wing span' if it fully outstretched its arms."

He was a skeptic before the sighting, but is not a skeptic anymore. It took him "a minimum of 60-90 seconds to regain control of my faculties" and continue his drive home.

Did they see a Bigfoot or was it simply a lumberjack without a neck? (Getty)

BIGFOOT IS A NEANDERTHAL-HUMAN HYBRID, ACCORDING TO THE MAN WHO CLAIMS TO HAVE FOUND REMAINS

This wasn't a bear caught in his high beams, he insists. It was a cryptid that walked in front of his car. That he is certain of. He spoke to two BFRO investigators and went on camera from the spot where he claims to have seen the Bigfoot.

While recalling his sighting, he was asked if he thought the Bigfoot he saw was male or female. He responded, "I, you know, I don't know... I'll say this, if the females are that big, I don't want to see a male."

Someone off camera, we can assume from the response he gave, asked if the Bigfoot he saw had boobs. The witness replied, "No, there were no boobs."

Some doubters of the viral footage claim that it shows nothing more than a Bigfoot yard display. (Getty Images/iStockphoto)

OUTKICK IS NOW ON THE FOX APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

Sometimes you have to ask the tough questions. Are we any closer to knowing the truth about Bigfoot based on this sighting?

I don't think we can answer that. Not at the moment anyway.

However, as long as we have people out there willing to investigate reports and ask the questions no one else is willing to, that includes whether the Bigfoot had boobs or not, we're headed in the right direction.

title: India’s Cockroach Janta party protest victory signals trouble ahead for Modi
excerpt:
Ally forced to resign, with opposition parties reinvigorated and strongman leader’s grip over media channels rocked

Even the night before Narendra Modi accepted the resignation of his education minis...
body_text:
Ally forced to resign, with opposition parties reinvigorated and strongman leader’s grip over media channels rocked

Even the night before Narendra Modi accepted the resignation of his education minister, India’s prime minister appeared confident that the largest mass uprising to take place in his 12 years in power would do little to rattle his government.

Addressing his “young friends” in a late-night Instagram selfie reel on Friday, he thanked the people – who were mobilised en masse across the country, shouting anti-government slogans – for their “thoughtful suggestions”.

Less than 24 hours later, Modi, who has fiercely cultivated his strongman image for years, had accepted Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation. It was, say analysts, the remarkable humbling of a government that has proved itself unwilling to bow in the face of any public pressure and which has ruled with almost untouchable impunity since 2014.

Over that past week, a gen Z movement that called itself the Cockroach Janta party (CJP) mobilised an unprecedented protest movement in the name of justice for millions of young people when the leaking of a crucial exam paper forced 2 million students to resit the test and was blamed for more than a dozen suicides.

The resignation of Pradhan, Modi’s loyal political ally, remained their first and foremost demand for accountability, even as the protests expanded into a wider fight for democracy. Yet Pradhan went unmentioned by Modi in his Instagram address.

On Saturday morning, more people than ever were pouring into Delhi’s historic Jantar Mantar site – the centre of the protests – and unrest was spreading fast to other cities, including states ruled by Modi’s Bharatiya Janata party (BJP).

It was not only physical space that had been captured by the cockroach movement. Since coming to power, the BJP has proved enormously effective at capturing the online narrative, deploying its powerful, highly organised IT cell to mobilise and attack any perceived criticism of the government, whether it came from citizens, politicians or journalists.

But this proved no match for the millions of gen Z memes and reels that began to flood Instagram over this past week, fearlessly insulting Modi and pillorying the government, each more creative and incendiary than the next. Modi’s last-ditch attempts to speak directly to the youth on Instagram were simply met with more ridicule and spin-off memes.

Modi had also lost another medium critical to the BJP’s domination over the national narrative – the mainstream TV news channels widely acknowledged to have been co-opted by the BJP government over the past 12 years and turned into mouthpieces for its rightwing Hindu nationalist ideology.

Initially, the channels ignored the protests, and when they did cover them it was to suggest the protesters were being bankrolled by sinister foreign forces and Pakistani terror groups. In response, the protesters turned on the channels, using social media to expose their “lies”. When the protests escalated, Modi remained conspicuously absent from the airwaves.

Pradhan’s resignation came as it appeared that all other options for the government had gone. The option of a ruthless crackdown appeared untenable given the mass outcry to the police violence that had hit protesters on Monday.

“The online space was totally conquered by the protesters and regime-loving media was seriously delegitimised,” said Ashutosh Varshney, a professor of international studies at Brown University in Rhode Island. “The anger was so comprehensive there was no option left but for Pradhan to go.”

But this was more than the loss of a minister, Varshney said, it was also the first time in 12 years that the Modi government had lost control of the political narrative. “This is a repressive government,” he said. “It wants obedience, it wants no critical discussion and it generates fear. But now the climate of fear has collapsed.”

Analysts say the resignation of Pradhan could also have implications for Modi’s power over his own cabinet. Pradhan was one of Modi’s most loyal ministers and ideological footsoldiers, and had implemented policies exactly as senior party figures had wanted. He had also helped the BJP win Odisha state for the first time in the general election, bringing in crucial seats.

“Modi knows once you start firing your most loyal ministers, it sets up the incentives for defections in other ministers as well,” said the political columnist Pratap Bhanu Mehta. “If your own cabinet starts to hedge for a future where they may not be backed by your own government, that’s when you are in trouble.”

Prior to this week’s unrest, Modi had been riding high on a string of important state electoral victories, in particular the BJP’s first triumph in West Bengal, a politically important state that had long pushed back against its Hindu nationalist politics.

The BJP appeared to have fully bounced back from the blow in the 2024 elections, when the party failed to win an outright parliamentary majority and had to scramble together a large enough alliance to take power. At the same time, the much-beleaguered opposition had continued to lose countless state elections and their allegations of voting impropriety by the BJP fell mostly on deaf ears.

Yet the emergence of the cockroaches has reinvigorated not only India’s youth, but its political opposition parties as well. Jumping on the bandwagon, the opposition Congress party has had its best week in years as it mobilised protests and shut down parliament. The party’s leader, Rahul Gandhi, was dramatically dragged away by police outside Modi’s house in support of students.

Analysts say that dissent, which had been systematically crushed over the past 12 years, has now been re-galvanised as an effective tool to hold the government to account.

“After a long time, there’s an assertion of political agency across different sections of society,” said Mehta. “And the minute you see that agency out in the street, it empowers lots of other agents.”

The next big test of the electoral implications of the CJP movement will come early next year, when India’s largest and most politically important state holds its state elections. Holding on to power in Uttar Pradesh, the BJP’s political heartland, is seen as crucial for the party and would have major implications for the next general election in 2029.

Just how the CJP intends to politically mobilise after its striking victory on Saturday remains to be seen. Leaders and supporters insist this is just the “beginning”, particularly in their push for education reform. Their founder, Abhijeet Dipke, has some past experience as a political party organiser, but has not made his own ambitions known.

Yet analysts said that one of the most crucial impacts of the CJP had been to reopen a rapidly closing democratic space and make it seem possible that a new kind of political opposition could emerge, one reflective of the voices heard on the streets of India this week.

Saurav Das, a CJP spokesperson, said it was encouraging people involved in the movement to go into politics. “This is one of our goals,” he said. “We need to increase youth participation in politics, because right now it’s controlled by uncles and aunties who are only interested in looking after their own lifestyles and don’t understand the needs of our generation. The answer also has to be political.”
