title: More than 250,000 flee wildfires in France and Spain
excerpt:
Firefighters battle flames in Lège-Cap-Ferret, south-western France

Firefighters are struggling to contain wildfires in south-west France as strong winds push flames towards the city of Bordeaux, wit...
body_text:
Firefighters battle flames in Lège-Cap-Ferret, south-western France

Firefighters are struggling to contain wildfires in south-west France as strong winds push flames towards the city of Bordeaux, with one official saying they "are far from having the fire under control."

More than 250,000 people in France and Spain have fled fires which have been raging for days, as winds and high temperatures hamper efforts to contain them. Overnight, seven towns west of Bordeaux were told to evacuate residents.

In Spain, where a state of emergency has been declared, a change in weather conditions has helped firefighters outside Madrid.

Spanish PM Pedro Sánchez admitted there are "complex times ahead". Meanwhile, authorities in València confirmed the death of a man in a fire.

The man, believed to be in his 70s, was found dead in his car by firefighters as they extinguished a fire in the Salt de l'Aigua ravine in Manises, according to local media reports.

In France, around 200,000 people have been evacuated in south-western regions of Gironde and Landes regions.

France has mobilised its military to help with the response and extra reinforcements from the army have been sent to help firefighters by clearing brush and creating fire breaks.

As of Saturday morning, the wildfire was around 40km to 50km (25 to 30 miles) away from Bordeaux. Still, the wind was blowing smoke towards the city and people reported an acrid smell in the air.

One tourist who fled an approaching wildfire near Bordeaux with his family described the scale of the blaze as "frightening".

Spencer Randall told the BBC his family evacuated in the early hours of Saturday to an area 100 miles east, but they can "still smell the wildfires from here".

"It's quite strong winds fanning the flames, just terrifying," he said.

Shelters have been set up across the region to house evacuees

A British couple holidaying in Bordeaux said they noticed the flames get worse on Friday night, as the fire approached.

"At about seven o'clock you could smell smoke. We thought someone was having a barbecue," Maisie told BBC Newsbeat from their holiday rental.

Her partner, Caleb, said the ash has now covered the pool in the house and turned their feet black when walking outside.

The smoke "really hits your lungs right away", they added.

Nearby, in Saint-Aubin-de-Médoc, residents evacuating said the situation was "stressful", with one local describing it a "disaster".

The final leg of the Tour de France, due to take place Sunday, has been shortened from 133km (83 miles) to 89km (55 miles) so that security forces can be redeployed to areas affected by wildfires, organisers and police have said.

French President Emmanuel Macron is set to have an emergency meeting with ministers as 30 or so fires rage across the country - a situation which the government said is totally unprecedented.

Watch: Anxiety as locals forced to evacuate Saint-Aubin-de-Médoc

In Spain, fires continued near Madrid but the regional government said there had been some progress.

"The change in weather conditions - less wind, higher humidity and lower temperature - has greatly benefited the fight against the forest fires, which have advanced little and decreased in intensity," it wrote on X.

Speaking from Cenicientos, south-west of Madrid, Prime Minister Sánchez said: "Right now, we have a window of opportunity in order to tackle against the wildfires, protect and save lives and effectively try and control the fire."

"It's true that temperatures have dropped a little bit. But still the wind is making it difficult and there may be thunderstorms as well."

Since the wildfires broke out in Spain, nearly 60,000 people have been evacuated from the Madrid and Ávila regions, while more than 28,000 remain confined to their homes, according to Spain's Interior Ministry.

Madrid's regional president Isabel Díaz Ayuso described the situation as the "worst fire in the history of the region".

Sánchez said 130,000 hectares of land had been burned in Spain so far this year, ahead of an annual average of 100,000 hectares for the country over the last decade.

A helicopter dumps water as firefighters collect water from a pool in El Tiemblo, outside Madrid

France's Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said 98,000 hectares have burned across the country since the beginning of 2026.

Meanwhile in Italy, more than 350 fires - including 10 major blazes - broke out on the island of Sicily, the head of the Sicilian Civil Protection said on Wednesday, prompting evacuations.

A major incident was also declared by emergency services in Scotland on Friday evening as they continue to tackle a wildfire in the Cairngorms National Park that has been burning for 10 days.

Hadja Lahbib, the EU's commissioner for crisis management, said it is likely that the damage from wildfires in Europe will surpass previous records.

Watch: Flames reach evacuated town outside Madrid

She said fires had started earlier in the year when, in April, the Netherlands activated the EU's civil protection mechanism which triggers support and reinforcements from other countries.

Lahbib told the BBC: "Last year, one million hectares burned during the summer and so we are expecting to face another historical, sad record because the season has started earlier in the year."

She also warned that more outbreaks are likely as the summer goes on.

"Forecasters are predicting, unfortunately, another heatwave so we can expect other wildfires," Lahbib added.

France has activated the civil protection mechanism and will receive water bombers, comprising three Canadairs planes from Croatia and two Air Tractors from Portugal, as well as Black Hawk helicopters from the Czech Republic and Slovakia, and 40 members of a Romanian forest fire team.

EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said 11 planes and helicopters have also been sent to France and Spain from the EU's firefighting fleet.

Additional reporting by Mary Litchfield, BBC Your Voice and Srosh Khan, BBC Newsbeat

Tourists tell BBC how their holiday turned into race to escape fires

'Upheaval' - French wildfire evacuations in the middle of the night

More than 220,000 evacuated in France and Spain due to wildfires

title: Fired school counselor loses again after free speech fight over gender-themed books in his office
excerpt: America First Legal Senior Counsel Ian Prior and Loudoun County parent Abbie Platt discuss gender ideology policies in schools. They reveal how these policies impact children, parental rights, and the...
body_text:
America First Legal Senior Counsel Ian Prior and Loudoun County parent Abbie Platt discuss gender ideology policies in schools. They reveal how these policies impact children, parental rights, and the legal battles faced by families opposing them.

A federal appeals court ruled earlier this week that a now-fired Oregon school counselor’s display of books promoting binary gender views to students was not protected by the First Amendment.

The 2-1 decision handed down by the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals on Tuesday upheld Roderick E. Theis II’s termination from Oregon’s InterMountain Education Service District (IMESD), according to court documents obtained by Fox News Digital.

CHICAGO COLLEGE REMOVES LGBTQ PRIDE FLAG OVER INSTITUTIONAL NEUTRALITY CONCERNS

Security guards stand in front of the Ninth U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals in San Francisco, Calif., on June 12, 2017. (Getty Images)

According to the ruling, Theis, an education specialist who worked for the IMESD for more than 15 years, displayed books titled "He is He" and "She is She" in two separate offices on different campuses when meeting with middle school students.

He also displayed a children’s book penned by conservative commentator Matt Walsh, titled "Johnny the Walrus," that "allegorically comments on transgender issues," court documents said.

Following an investigation into the incident, Theis told school administrators that he did not mean any harm by displaying the books and even considered putting them away when transgender-identifying students visited his office.

WISCONSIN TEACHER FIRED AFTER SOCIAL MEDIA POST ADVOCATING TO 'MAKE AMERICANS GREAT ASSASSINS AGAIN'

The InterMountain Education Service District in Oregon, where Roderick E. Theis II worked for more than 15 years as an education specialist serving middle school students. (Google Maps)

However, IMESD concluded the display of the books was a "bias incident" and instructed the counselor to remove them from his school offices — or risk termination.

A federal judge later partially granted Theis’ request for a protective order that allowed him to continue displaying the books in his offices when students were not visiting, but his employment was ultimately terminated after a district investigation revealed Theis provided the books to middle school students who had requested to see them, according to the ruling.

Theis’ attorneys went on to argue that the counselor was protected from the injunction when meeting with students outside of their official sessions, but a lower court later ruled that the partial injunction prohibited Theis from displaying the books when students were present in his office.

GOP LAWMAKERS URGE SUPREME COURT TO STRENGTHEN FIRST AMENDMENT PROTECTIONS FOR STREET PREACHERS

The 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals upheld the firing of Oregon school counselor Roderick E. Theis II over his display of books promoting binary gender views to middle school students. (iStock)

The lower court, however, issued another ruling against Theis’ termination appeal.

The ruling was upheld by the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals on Tuesday, with the majority opinion outlining longstanding precedents that an educators’ speech is considered government speech when interacting with students.

"As a government employee, Theis was assigned to work in school offices, meet with students, and carry out his duties in that setting," Circuit Judge John B. Owens wrote in the majority ruling. "His speech occurred in the course of those responsibilities and cannot be meaningfully separated from them. As such, Theis’s speech falls outside the First Amendment’s ambit."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

The sole dissenting opinion, written by Circuit Judge Lawrence VanDyke, sharply criticized the ruling. VanDyke argued that Theis’ books should be considered personal decorative items in his office, while questioning if a school could permit employees to hang pro-Palestinian banners while simultaneously banning the display of the Israeli flag.

"Could public school administrators establish a policy allowing office decoration with partisan political messages deemed sufficiently ‘compassionate,’ but prohibit — as inherently hostile’ — any political speech that did not align with the Democratic Socialists of America platform?" VanDyke wrote.

Fox News Digital reached out to Theis’ attorney and the IMESD for comment.

Julia Bonavita is a media and culture writer for Fox News Digital, and a Fox Flight Team drone pilot. You can follow her at @juliabonavita13 on all platforms and send story tips to julia.bonavita@fox.com.

title: The biggest food and drink mistakes travelers make on flights, experts warn
excerpt: Fox News senior medical analyst Dr. Marc Siegel reveals the best and worst drinks and foods to stay hydrated in hot weather. He details why water, coconut water and fruits are good, while soda and ene...
body_text:
Fox News senior medical analyst Dr. Marc Siegel reveals the best and worst drinks and foods to stay hydrated in hot weather. He details why water, coconut water and fruits are good, while soda and energy drinks should be avoided.

Flying can take a toll on the body in many ways, but experts say there are simple nutrition rules travelers should follow to reduce common problems like bloating, dehydration, dry skin and fatigue.

Air travel exposes travelers to changes in cabin humidity, pressure and oxygen levels that can affect overall comfort, with the dry cabin air being the biggest contributor to dehydration.

In addition to thirst, dehydration can cause headaches, low energy, muscle cramps and dizziness. In more severe cases, it can also lead to confusion and fainting.

Travelers should consume protein-rich snacks and avoid foods laden with salt or sugar, experts say. (iStock)

Travelers are prone to making several mistakes that contribute to dehydration, experts say. Many people avoid consuming liquids when they travel to cut down on bathroom breaks.

Some are also likely to opt for foods that are salty, greasy and heavy. It's also common to load up on caffeine and alcohol, which can contribute to bloating, constipation, dehydration and electrolyte imbalance.

Health experts advise hydrating before, during and after a flight. Bring your own water bottle that you can sip slowly and refill, so you don’t have to rely on onboard beverages.

"By the time you feel thirsty, your body is already dehydrated," Lindsay Baker, a director at the Gatorade Sports Science Institute, told Eating Well. "It is better to plan ahead and make sure you are well-hydrated before you start your trip. This helps avoid the need to drink large volumes of fluid to ‘catch up’ on hydration later."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Drinking water alone may not be enough, according to Baker.

"Your body needs electrolytes to hold onto the water you’re drinking," she said.

Electrolytes are naturally found in foods like bananas, spinach and avocados and are also available in drink mixes and tablets.

Carbonated drinks, such as soda, sparkling water and beer, also make bloating worse by adding gas to the stomach.

Alcohol, and excessive caffeine intake, may contribute to dehydration and are best avoided when flying, experts say.

Alcohol can make the dehydration caused by air travel worse, experts warn. (iStock)

"If you do want to drink alcohol, opt for something like a single Bloody Mary — tomato juice is a source of electrolytes as well as being antioxidant rich," Stephanie Smith, a women’s health nutritionist for Agora Health, told CNT Travler.

The reduced cabin pressure on airplanes can cause gas in the digestive tract to expand, leading to bloating. To minimize this effect, experts advise avoiding gas-producing foods, such as beans, lentils, broccoli, cabbage, onions and Brussels sprouts.

Eat smaller, lighter meals, since large, heavy meals slow digestion and leave more food sitting in the stomach.

Overly sweet and salty foods should also be avoided. High-sodium foods can increase thirst and may contribute to temporary bloating during flights.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"I suggest people avoid snacks high in simple carbohydrates or added sugars without other macronutrients to properly balance them out," Marra Burroughs, a doctor of clinical nutrition and registered dietitian, told Travel + Leisure.

"Traveling is exhausting to begin with, and a poorly balanced carb-heavy snack can lead to a crash that can worsen the experience and add to fatigue," Burroughs added. "If you want to partake in a snack that is higher in sugar, I recommend pairing it with fat and protein to balance it out."

Water-rich foods, such as fresh fruits and vegetables, are healthy food options while flying, according to nutritionists. (iStock)

It’s best to steer clear of ultra-processed snacks at the airport and choose protein-forward options such as unsalted nuts, Greek yogurt, cheese sticks and hard-boiled eggs.

Nutrient-dense water-rich foods such as watermelon, grapes, cucumbers and celery can also help travelers stay hydrated.

Flying on an empty stomach is also a bad idea, experts say, because low blood sugar can contribute to fatigue, irritability and dizziness during travel. Eating a well-balanced meal a couple of hours before a flight is advised.

Teresa Mull is a freelance writer with the Lifestyle team at Fox News Digital.

title: Tony Romo's brutal golf score before getting arrested paints a nightmarish picture
excerpt: Bodycam footage of Tiger Woods' March 27 DUI arrest in Jupiter Island, FL, shows a dazed and disoriented Woods after his rollover crash. Criminal defense attorney Donna Rotunno analyzes the video, inc...
body_text:
Bodycam footage of Tiger Woods' March 27 DUI arrest in Jupiter Island, FL, shows a dazed and disoriented Woods after his rollover crash. Criminal defense attorney Donna Rotunno analyzes the video, including Woods' claim of talking to the President, and discusses the legal hurdles for prosecutors to prove impairment, especially with no positive alcohol test.

Yes, Tony Romo is making headlines, again, for all the wrong reasons ahead of this 2026 NFL season.

For those who missed it, the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback was arrested in Milwaukee Thursday night for allegedly operating while intoxicated.

TONY ROMO ARRESTED IN MILWAUKEE FOR ALLEGED OWI OFFENSE: REPORT

Romo was reportedly stopped on a highway and performed poorly on field sobriety tests, FOX6 in Milwaukee reported. He was released and is due in court Sept. 21.

Tony Romo plays his shot from the second tee box during the final round of the American Century Championship at Edgewood Tahoe Golf Course in Stateline, Nevada, on July 13, 2025. (Eakin Howard/Getty Images)

I'm not here to break down the Xs and Os of Romo's arrest, and what it might mean for his future at CBS. I don't care about that. I care about what Romo was doing before his ill-fated drive home.

FORMER COWBOYS QB TONY ROMO FALLS SHORT IN US OPEN GOLF QUALIFYING BID

The 46-year-old was arrested on the same day as the final round of the Wisconsin Amateur Championship golf tournament. Romo is an excellent golfer, and was playing in the event. Last week, he played in the American Century Championship celebrity golf tournament.

His offseasons are mostly spent on a golf course, which is fair. It's where I'd be, too.

Here's the thing ... this particular event didn't go great for Romo. Boots on the ground reported that he finished the tournament a whopping 35-over par and won just $60.

Look, I'm not gonna rag on Romo for a bad few days of golf. He's an elite golfer — for an amateur — and I am awful. I usually sit around 85, and that's only if my short game cooperates.

That being said, it's still wild to see a +35 on the scorecard. Lordy.

Tony Romo mugshot from arrest. (Fox News Digital)

Now, the course was obviously a hornets nest. I know this because a quick Google search tells me the winner finished at +3. The cut-line was +15. Sounds like a nightmare. Frankly, it sounds like I'd blow through a dozen Noodles before the turn. Maybe more.

But man, seeing Tony Romo card a +35 and then get pulled over for operating while under the influence is a doozy. I'm not sitting here condoning drinking and then driving, obviously. That's a big no-no. It should never happen in this day in age. There are Ubers on every corner, even in West Bend, Wisconsin.

After shooting a 12-over in the final round, though? Tough look.

title: Iran’s government spars with state TV as mediators push talks with US
excerpt: Tehran, Iran – A public rift has emerged between Iran’s government and state television over how to portray the state of war and negotiations with the United States, as mediators try to nudge both cou...
body_text:
Tehran, Iran – A public rift has emerged between Iran’s government and state television over how to portray the state of war and negotiations with the United States, as mediators try to nudge both countries towards diplomacy.

The Government Information Council on Friday accused state broadcaster IRIB of “censorship” after parts of a speech by President Masoud Pezeshkian earlier in the week were not shown to the public.

The broadcaster, whose head is appointed by the supreme leader, issued a response on Saturday rejecting the government’s “accusations and improper attributions”, and emphasised that it has a duty to prevent “an incorrect and unreal suggestion of duality in the country’s leadership pillars”.

In his speech, Pezeshkian had pointed out that after last year’s 12-day war with Israel, former Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei publicly said there would be no negotiations with Washington – but privately had given his approval.

“We went to the dear leader, explained the situation, and asked him what to do since he had said the ‘no war, no peace’ conditions are bad for the country,” the president said. “He ordered us to go negotiate. We started the talks based on his order.”

The government said in its statement the move to cut that section of the speech was part of a series of “unusual actions” taken by state television concerning recent comments made by the heads of the government, parliament and judiciary.

It pointed out that earlier this month, a part of the parliament speaker and chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf’s interview with state television dealing with negotiations had also been cut. The government council added that a part of a speech earlier this week by judiciary head Gholam-Hossein Mohseni-Ejei was not aired either, in which he expressed backing for the president.

Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has also separately criticised IRIB, saying during an interview with a state-linked outlet released on Saturday that he “fought with a sword” in wartime interviews with US media such as Fox, CNN and others. The chief diplomat said he expected state television to show how Iran’s case was being strongly presented to US audiences and policymakers, but only one or two subtitles from the interviews ended up going on air.

Araghchi also rejected a notion raised by hardliners that the now-suspended memorandum of understanding signed with the US last month was “imposed” on new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, as some hardliners have claimed. He characterised it as the best possible agreement under the circumstances.

In its own statement, the government blamed the actions on “a political faction within” state television, in an apparent reference to the Paydari Front of ultrahardliners, and said their actions could serve to undermine national security and social cohesion.

IRIB, in a statement published by its public relations department, countered that broadcasting the president’s segment would have propagated an appearance of division.

Both sides accused each other of undermining the decree issued last week by Mojtaba Khamenei to reach a “sacred unity” in face of military, economic and diplomatic pressure by the US.

Mohammad Mirzaei, a member of parliament and spokesperson of a committee tasked with exerting oversight on IRIB, said on Saturday that directors of the state broadcaster have been warned about the necessity to display different viewpoints and to act as a “sign of national unity”.

Conservative journalist Mohammad Mohajeri told local media that the broadcaster is now at its most expensive and least effective. Reformist activist Mohammad-Sadegh Javadi-Hesar described the deeper problem as “one government being installed and another government called IRIB operating against it”.

Reformist Entekhab news outlet reported, citing an unnamed source, that Pezeshkian sharply reprimanded IRIB chief Peyman Jebeli at a cabinet meeting after the row over the negotiations. Jebeli, who was appointed by Ali Khamenei in 2021, was media deputy at the Supreme National Security Council when Saeed Jalili, the only council member said to have voted against an interim deal with the US last month, was its secretary.

Hardline lawmaker Meysam Zohourian said the president has threatened to cut state television’s budget, but the administration has not confirmed this.

As the public sparring unfolded, mediators from Oman were in Tehran on Friday to discuss the management of the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway whose control has become a central point of contention between the US and Iran.

US President Donald Trump argued on Friday the war was going “extremely well” and that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will visit Washington in the coming days.

He said the two sides continued to talk through mediators, but that he did not expect any agreement soon.

The US president also refused to answer whether realising his threat of systematically attacking power plants and bridges in Iran in case of a war escalation would constitute war crimes.

Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr, the secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, on Saturday responded by saying missile and drone launches across the region will continue “until the full surrender of the enemy” and avenging the blood of civilians killed during the war.

title: Worker dies during reconstruction of Barcelona’s Camp Nou Stadium
excerpt:
Barcelona football club say a construction worker has died during renovations at their Camp Nou stadium.

In a short statement published on Saturday, the Spanish club said it “deeply regrets the death...
body_text:
Barcelona football club say a construction worker has died during renovations at their Camp Nou stadium.

In a short statement published on Saturday, the Spanish club said it “deeply regrets the death of the worker who lost his life yesterday in the workplace accident”.

The club expressed its condolences to his family, friends and co-workers.

Catalan police said the 54-year-old worker died from a blow to the head. No further details on the circumstances were given when queried by The Associated Press news agency.

Barcelona started a major overhaul of Camp Nou, Europe’s largest football stadium, in 2023. Players returned to the venue in November, with a limited seating capacity for fans, as construction work continued.

The Catalan club have won Spain’s La Liga title for the last two seasons and begin their new campaign on August 23 at Elche.

Their first home game at Camp Nou, which has been partially reopened for the last year during the works, is against Athletic Bilbao on August 27.

The capacity for the ground when finished will be 105,000, making it the largest in Europe.

title: More than 250,000 people flee wildfires in France and Spain
excerpt:
Hundreds of firefighters battle blazes as strong winds drive fires towards Bordeaux and smoke prompts health warnings in Madrid

Unrestrained wildfires in Spain and France have forced more than 250,00...
body_text:
Hundreds of firefighters battle blazes as strong winds drive fires towards Bordeaux and smoke prompts health warnings in Madrid

Unrestrained wildfires in Spain and France have forced more than 250,000 people to flee, authorities from both countries have said, as they struggle to contain the blazes.

About 70,000 people were evacuated from central Spain, while 197,000 people fled in France, including tens of thousands from the wine region city of Bordeaux.

Spain declared a national emergency, the first time the country has ever done so over a wildfire. France’s evacuations constituted “probably” the biggest peacetime evacuation the country has ever seen, its interior minister said.

Hundreds of firefighters have worked to contain the blazes, which have been fuelled by persistent heatwaves and the climate crisis, but were still unable to stop their advance. In Spain, high winds were exacerbating the fires, and two of the three blazes merged on Friday.

France’s interior minister, Laurent Nuñez, said a huge military cargo plane, the Airbus A400M Atlas, was being deployed to join 18 other aircraft in the “long and very difficult” battle against wildfires in the Gironde region of south-western France.

The French government has called in the military to help, deploying 1,500 soldiers, and has rushed 1.5m face masks to help protect people from smoke inhalation. Fire crews have also been digging trenches, as well as using retardants, as winds were forecast to push the fires closer to Bordeaux. Wildfires were reported to be about 20 miles west of the city.

The French government ordered people in the path of the fire to evacuate, including those in Bordeaux’s western suburbs. Police went door to door to tell people to leave, with scenes of panic unfolding as residents fled their homes under a smoke-darkened sky.

The Gironde regional prefect, Sophie Brocas, said on Friday that strong winds were driving the fire towards the Bordeaux metro area and that it had grown to “an unprecedented magnitude”.

Officials said the sudden blazes caught residents and authorities off guard. Some people in France had to flee by boat when the flames headed towards coastal towns.

The French prime minister, Sébastien Lecornu, said the fire in Gironde was so strong that it had begun generating its own winds.

“The fires that are hitting our country have reached a level that has never been seen before,” he wrote on X. “Our priority is clear: protecting human lives.” He urged people to obey evacuation orders “without delay”.

The Spanish health minister instructed people in Madrid not to go outside over concern of the poor air quality.

“Avoid physical activity and staying outdoors. If you go outdoors and there is smoke or ash, use a mask,” Monica Garcia said on X.

On Saturday evening, Spain’s interior ministry said a man had died in a fire in Manises, in Valencia. He had been found in a car in a ravine, officials said.

The fire was a separate incident from the major blazes raging west of Madrid, which have so far not caused any reported deaths.

The long, back-to-back heatwaves in Europe have dried forests out, turning them into tinder for wildfires. Fires had already consumed 130,000 hectares (320,000 acres) of forest this year in Spain, about a third higher than the country’s annual average, Spain’s prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, said on Saturday.

In France, fires burned down more than 98,000 hectares, which France’s interior minister said was a “historic record”.

Scientists say climate breakdown is triggering more frequent and more extreme weather events, evaporating soils and waterways, fuelling wildfires and leading to thousands of excess deaths. Europe is heating at about twice the global average rate.

Sánchez said that cooler weather on Saturday gave a “window of opportunity” for firefighters to help contain the blazes. “We are going to have some complex hours ahead because, although the temperatures have gone down, we do not know exactly how the wind will develop, how strong it will be,” he added.

Other European countries were helping both countries fight the blazes, with Croatia, the Czech Republic, Greece, Italy, the Netherlands, Portugal and Slovakia sending aid and water-dumping aircraft to France and Spain.

The European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, promised more help was on the way.

“Europe stands alongside France and Spain in the face of the devastating wildfires ravaging them. Five planes and two helicopters from the rescue fleet are now deployed in France and four planes are arriving in Spain today,” she said on X.

title: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan suffers significant injuries in offseason car wreck
excerpt: Albert Breer joins Colin Cowherd to break down the biggest games of the NFL season, featuring the Chicago Bears' early schedule, the San Francisco 49ers' travels, Dallas Cowboys and Las Vegas Raiders'...
body_text:
Albert Breer joins Colin Cowherd to break down the biggest games of the NFL season, featuring the Chicago Bears' early schedule, the San Francisco 49ers' travels, Dallas Cowboys and Las Vegas Raiders' lack of prime time games. He then dives into A...

San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shananhan was involved in a serious car wreck last week, the team announced on Saturday.

Shanahan broke his nose, three ribs, his hand, needed over 40 stitches in his face and suffered a severe concussion in the accident, according to ESPN. The incident happened on July 14 when the 45-year-old coach collided with another SUV by his home in northern California, according to the report.

"San Francisco 49ers Head Coach Kyle Shanahan was involved in a car accident last week where he suffered non-life-threatening injuries. Coach Shanahan will participate in team activities on a limited basis at the start of training camp while he recovers. Coach Shanahan and the 49ers organization would like to sincerely thank all first responders involved for their efforts and care," the 49ers said in a statement.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan watches from the sideline during the second half of an NFL football game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Tampa, Florida, on Oct. 12, 2025. (AP Photo/Chris O'Meara)

"Assistant Head Coach Chris Foerster along with team coordinators will handle head coach responsibilities during this period."

Palo Alto lieutenant Nicholas Martinez told ESPN that the other driver was not injured and that drugs or alcohol were not involved. Shanahan was taken to the hospital by local paramedics after the wreck and was released after spending much of the day there.

"Consistent with our standard release of information procedures in such cases, we do not release information regarding the cause of the collision, or which party may have been at fault," Martinez told ESPN.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan calls a play during the game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara, California, on Sept. 28, 2025. (Brooke Sutton/Getty Images)

He told the outlet that no one was cited for the collision.

The 49ers' training camp starts on Sunday, but Shanahan will not be allowed to participate until he is cleared by doctors. The longtime coach told his assistant coaches about the accident on Tuesday, according to the report.

Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay, left, greets San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan after an NFL football game, Sunday, Sept. 22, 2024, in Inglewood, Calif.  (AP Photo/Ashley Landis)

Shanahan is entering his 10th season as the 49ers head coach and is widely considered one of the best coaches in the NFL. Over nine seasons, he has an 82-67 record and has led the team to the Super Bowl twice.

Shanahan is believed to be recovering well and healing at home, according to the report. The 49ers' first game of the season is against the Los Angeles Rams on Sept. 10 in Melbourne, Australia.

title: Elderly Florida man faces charges after alleged 'sugar baby' dispute ends in car-ramming, gun threat: police
excerpt:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

body_text:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A 67-year-old man's search for a "sugar baby" ended with him allegedly pointing a rifle at a 22-year-old after ramming a car into a telephone pole, according to his arrest report.

David Allen O'Brien, who lives in The Villages, a sprawling retirement community in central Florida, was arrested Tuesday on charges of aggravated assault after allegedly chasing down a 21-year-old woman he had paid in a "sugar baby" arrangement and ramming her car with his truck, according to the arrest report.

The arrest report details how O'Brien met the woman on the dating app Tinder and told her he was "looking for a sugar baby," a romantic arrangement that typically involves an older man spending lavishly on a younger woman.

FLORIDA MAN WHO ALLEGEDLY LURED WOMEN WITH DATING APP COULD HAVE MORE VICTIMS: AUTHORITIES

The pair agreed to meet on July 21 and O'Brien told the woman that he would give her $1,000 "each visit... dinner and I love to shop for you," according to the affidavit.

David Allen O'Brien is seen in a mugshot photo released by the Sumter County Sheriff's Office. (Sumter County Sheriff's Office)

The woman showed up to dinner with three friends waiting in the car, according to the affidavit.

When she arrived, O'Brien gave the woman $200 and took her shopping for lingerie. They then went to dinner, where he gave her another $600. Afterward, they went back to his home where she "began to feel uncomfortable and contacted her friends to come pick her up," the arrest report reads.

FLORIDA MAN WHO ALLEGEDLY LURED WOMEN WITH DATING APP COULD HAVE MORE VICTIMS: AUTHORITIES

"The defendant stated he began to massage [the woman's] feet and she was on her phone the entire time. The defendant advised [the woman] went to the bathroom and when she came out she stated she was going to call an Uber to pick her up," the report reads.

O'Brien then told the woman she "should give the money back because that was not the agreement," the report reads. She got into her friends' car, at which point O'Brien allegedly began chasing them in his Ford F-150 truck.

O'Brien allegedly rammed his date's car with his Ford F-150, causing them to crash into a telephone pole.

When the four friends reached a traffic circle, O'Brien rammed their car with his truck, forcing it to crash into a telephone pole, according to the affidavit. Three of then fled their vehicles, but when the fourth, a 22-year-old male, attempted to leave, he was met with O'Brien allegedly pointing a gun in his face.

FLORIDA MAN WHO ALLEGEDLY LURED WOMEN WITH DATING APP COULD HAVE MORE VICTIMS: AUTHORITIES

"The defendant pointed his 22 semi-automatic Ruger at him and told him to get on the ground or he would kill him," the arrest report read.

The man "was on the ground face down and noticed that the defendant was distracted so he was able to move to safety," the report also read.

When police arrived on the scene, they found O'Brien at his truck with his weapon in possession, according to the arrest report.

O'Brien claimed the car he was chasing had its tail lights blacked out, a sign, to him, that meant he had been "scammed," according to the arrest report.

O'Brien and the 21-year-old woman met on the dating app Tinder, according to the police report. The pair later began texting. (iStock)

O'Brien was charged with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without the intent to kill and aggravated battery. He was transferred to Sumter County Jail "without incident," per the arrest report.

His arraignment will take place on Aug. 14, according to Sumter County records.

Fox News Digital contacted the Sumter County Sheriff's Office for additional details.

title: Sophie Cunningham sees support surge after star puts career on line for girls' sports
excerpt:
The WNBA finally has momentum. The question is whether it knows how to use it.

Riley Gaines praised WNBA star Sophie Cunningham on Friday, calling her a rare voice of courage for speaking out against...
body_text:
The WNBA finally has momentum. The question is whether it knows how to use it.

Riley Gaines praised WNBA star Sophie Cunningham on Friday, calling her a rare voice of courage for speaking out against biological men competing in women's sports despite competing in what Gaines called the "most woke league of all time."

Gaines, a former NCAA swimmer and host of "The Riley Gaines Show," applauded Cunningham's refusal to back down on protecting female locker rooms and called her the "first current high-level female athlete" in a professional league to take such a stance.

"It's easy to say that men aren't women and men shouldn't play in women's sports. I'm here to tell you, if you're in Sophie Cunningham's position, it's not easy to say that. It's incredibly difficult. It requires immense courage," Gaines said.

"If you're Sophie Cunningham playing in the WNBA, which is like the most woke league of all time in the history of ever, it takes immense courage to say exactly what she did. And it makes her really the first current high-level female athlete playing in a professional league that has said this."

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM DOUBLES DOWN AHEAD OF SUN GAME AFTER ESPN PROFILE STIRS CONTROVERSY: 'I SAID WHAT I SAID'

Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham plays in the second half against the Los Angeles Sparks at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in Indianapolis, Ind., on June 27, 2026. (Trevor Ruszkowski/Imagn Images)

Earlier this week, Cunningham revealed her stance on transgender athletes competing in women’s sports, telling ESPN, "I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans. And I'm like, 'I never once said that.'"

"I think that I am here to extend love. But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sports who shouldn't have to go against biological men," Cunningham said.

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SENDS MESSAGE TO HER HATERS AFTER SAYING MEN DON'T BELONG IN WOMEN'S SPORTS

Since her comments surfaced, Cunningham has received support online from various Republican lawmakers and advocates for women's sports, including Sens. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, and Eric Schmitt. R-Mo.

Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham smiles after falling Friday, May 15, 2026, during the second half of a game at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in Indianapolis. The Washington Mystics defeated the Indiana Fever in overtime, 104-102. (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect)

Gaines said she doesn't believe Cunningham is in it for the praise, noting that her opinion could actually cost the Indiana Fever star opportunities.

"And to be very clear, I don't think Sophie is doing or saying what she does because she wants fame," Gaines said.

WHITE HOUSE DEFENDS WNBA STAR SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM AFTER SHE SPEAKS OUT IN SUPPORT OF PROTECTING WOMEN'S SPORTS

"I'll put myself in her shoes. You have to imagine that she was concerned that she would lose opportunities. Maybe still she's even concerned about that. But she said it, and she stood by it because she thinks that's the right and the moral and the just thing to do," she added.

Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham reacts after scoring during the second half of a WNBA game against the Seattle Storm on Sunday, May 17, 2026, at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect)

Jennifer Sey, the CEO of pro-women's sportswear brand XX-XY Athletics, revealed to Fox News Digital that she wants to sign Cunningham to the brand, calling her the "perfect person for us."

"It’s not just that she’s a fantastic athlete, and she's a currently competing professional athlete," Sey said. "She’s just got such an incredible personality. She's fun, and she's funny, and she's tough, and she says what she thinks, and that's what we're all about."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Sey revealed that she first connected with Cunningham after XX-XY Athletics released its "Dear Nike" ad in October 2024. The ad challenged the sportswear giant to take a public stand against biological males competing in women's sports and generated more than 10 million views.

According to Sey, Cunningham liked and commented on the original ad, then sent her a private direct message on social media praising it. But Sey said she did not see the message for months because it landed in a folder for messages from accounts she did not follow.

Fox News’s Jackson Thompson contributed to this report.

Madison Colombo is a writer for Fox News Digital’s Flash, Media, and Culture team, covering daily breaking news and trending topics with an award-winning background in broadcast and digital journalism.

Ishan Kishan scored 81 and Ti...
body_text:
India ‌inflicted another heavy defeat on Zimbabwe when they ⁠won the ⁠second Twenty20 international at Harare Sports Club by 90 runs to secure their three-match ⁠series.

Ishan Kishan scored 81 and Tilak Varma an unbeaten 60 as India amassed a formidable total of ⁠219-5 after being put into bat before dismissing Zimbabwe cheaply for 129 to secure the victory on Saturday.

Kishan, whose runs came off 44 balls, and Tilak, who took 29 balls to get ‌to 60, accelerated the scoring in the middle overs, taking advantage of bowling that was often too full.

They put on 94 off 44 balls for the fourth wicket before Ishan was caught in the deep mistiming a slog at a wide delivery.

Zimbabwe faced ⁠a record run chase and, although ⁠opener Brian Bennett offered some early hope, they were always up against it and were dismissed in 17.5 overs.

Bennett played an array of ⁠strokes for 32 runs off 19 balls before falling to Yash Thakur, who ⁠finished with 2-30 on his T20 ⁠international debut.

Once Bennett had been dismissed, there was a steady fall of wickets, with the slow left-arm bowling of Abhishek Sharma producing the ‌best figures of 3-17.

India won the opening match of the three-game series at the Harare Sports Club by ‌seven ‌wickets with 40 balls to spare.

title: Sammy Hagar buries decades-long feud with David Lee Roth after tour dates are axed
excerpt:
Sammy Hagar doesn’t feel old yet and explains why he has no plans to retire.

David Lee Roth's summer comeback has hit an unexpected roadblock.

Several of the former Van Halen frontman's scheduled to...
body_text:
Sammy Hagar doesn’t feel old yet and explains why he has no plans to retire.

David Lee Roth's summer comeback has hit an unexpected roadblock.

Several of the former Van Halen frontman's scheduled tour dates were abruptly canceled, prompting fans to wonder what caused the shake-up.

As news of the cancellations spread, Sammy Hagar wasted no time reaching out publicly to his longtime Van Halen counterpart with an emotional message of support.

SAMMY HAGAR ADMITS HE WOULDN’T BE AS ‘LEGENDARY’ WITHOUT VAN HALEN

Sammy Hagar and David Lee Roth are seen during their tour in 2002. (SGranitz/WireImage)

"Hey Dave, Sammy here. I just got a call from Michael Anthony as I'm sitting down having my favorite cocktail, and I don't have to tell you what this is," Hagar said, smiling as he held up his signature margarita, "about your tour getting canceled."

"And I want to say from the bottom of my heart, I'm sorry. I hope you're well. I hope there's not a physical problem."

Shows in Colorado, Iowa, Kentucky and Illinois have all been canceled. No reason has been announced.

Only Roth's July dates have been scrapped. His five shows scheduled for August and September are currently still available for purchase through Ticketmaster, while his Aug. 7 performance in Sturgis, South Dakota, remains listed on his official website.

LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

David Lee Roth and Sammy Hagar present the Best Rock Video award at the 2002 MTV Video Music Awards. (Kevin Kane/WireImage)

"Honestly, Mike and I love the fact that you've been out there doing it, supporting the greatest band in the world that we were both part of," Hagar said. "And, yeah, I'm really sorry. That's f---ed up. Supporting what we did in this band to keep this music alive."

He also reflected on the chemistry that made Van Halen one of rock's defining acts.

"You and I, Mikey, Al, Ed, cannot be replaced."

JON BON JOVI ABRUPTLY ENDS MADISON SQUARE GARDEN SHOW AFTER HEALTH SETBACK

Hagar then encouraged Roth to return whenever he's ready.

"So, when you're ready to carry on, you go, brother. Mike and I support you."

Hagar extended an open invitation for Roth to join him and Michael Anthony during their Las Vegas residency this September.

Rock musicians Michael Anthony, Sammy Hagar, Eddie Van Halen and Alex Van Halen pose for a portrait in 1986. (Paul Natkin/Getty Images)

"Come to Vegas for the residency in September. Come on, join us. Sing a couple songs, MC the damn show. Come out and just do what the f--- you do, which is pretty damn entertaining."

He closed the video with a heartfelt sendoff.

"Anyway, hope you're well. I really do. God bless, brother."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

Hagar doubled down on the sentiment in the caption accompanying the video, writing:

"I'm looking rough, but who cares I'm serious with this post. I hope the news about Dave is not AI!!!!! if it is, my post is still coming from my heart and soul. It is so important that this music carry on especially with the AI music out there. those of us that can still go out and play. should do it as long as they can physically and emotionally carry that torch. @vanhalen was, should be, and hopefully always will be real live music, not just for our fans, but for the future fans of real rock music."

The public support marked a notable turn for the two rock icons, whose relationship has long been defined by competition.

Roth and Hagar both acted as the frontman for Van Halen at different times. (Fin Costello/Redferns)

After Roth exited Van Halen in 1985, Hagar stepped in as the band's new frontman alongside Eddie Van Halen, Alex Van Halen and Michael Anthony. Hagar remained with the group until 1996 and later returned from 2003 to 2005. Roth reclaimed the mic full-time in 2006, remaining with Van Halen until the band's final chapter in 2020.

Though they each defined different eras of Van Halen, Hagar and Roth spent decades trading public jabs. They briefly joined forces for the 2002 "Song for Song, The Heavyweight Champs of Rock and Roll" tour, but the truce was short-lived as their rivalry quickly reignited.

The canceled dates mark another twist in Roth's return to live performance after he stunned fans by announcing his retirement in 2021.

"I am throwing in the shoes. I'm retiring," he told the Las Vegas Review-Journal. "This is the first, and only, official announcement."

His planned farewell Las Vegas residency was later scrapped amid COVID-19-related circumstances, but Roth ultimately returned to the stage in 2025 and continued to perform into 2026.

He has not publicly addressed the canceled dates or responded to Hagar's invitation.

Fox News Digital reached out to Roth and Hagar for comment.

Stephanie Giang-Paunon is an entertainment reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: New North Sea oil drilling faces delay after gear accidentally dropped in sea
excerpt:
Exclusive: Blunder at Rosebank, UK’s biggest undeveloped oilfield, comes as government considers granting licence

Production at Britain’s biggest undeveloped oil and gasfield could be delayed for mon...
body_text:
Exclusive: Blunder at Rosebank, UK’s biggest undeveloped oilfield, comes as government considers granting licence

Production at Britain’s biggest undeveloped oil and gasfield could be delayed for months after equipment from a rig was accidentally dropped in the North Sea, the Guardian can reveal.

Andy Burnham’s new government is under pressure from the fossil fuel industry to allow oil to be retrieved from the Rosebank site despite opposition from climate campaigners and some Labour MPs.

Rosebank, located about 80 miles north-west of Shetland, was believed to be ready to generate oil before the end of the year, pending ministerial approval.

Adura, the company responsible for Rosebank, now says it anticipates this will happen at some point in 2027. The field is projected to produce 300m barrels of oil over its 25-year lifespan, according to industry estimates.

Some MPs believe enhanced domestic production of oil and gas would help tackle the cost of living, a central focus of the new prime minister, by improving energy security amid global instability, while green campaigners believe the impact on the UK economy of exploiting the fields would be minimal.

However, delays at Rosebank mean production at the field will be unlikely to affect the UK’s energy supply over the winter months. Licences for Rosebank and another site, Jackdaw, were granted under the Conservatives but operations were paused after a court challenge by environmental groups.

The new energy secretary, Miatta Fahnbulleh, is expected to make a decision on the fields’ future after consultations regarding their emissions conclude in August.

Earlier this week, Adura told the BBC that the Jackdaw site, about 150 miles east of Aberdeen, could produce gas as early as October.

However, preparations for oil production at Rosebank have been hindered by the rig incident, which occurred on 18 April. No workers were hurt, but two central pieces of drilling equipment, including a safety valve, were dropped 1,100 metres on to the seabed.

The platform, hired by Adura from Norwegian company Odfjell Drilling, was taken to a shipyard in Bergen for repairs. It is now back at Rosebank but not yet operational.

Odfjell Drilling said in internal documentation that the rig could be out of action for up to four months. The Guardian understands this means that some oil wells will be completed significantly behind schedule.

Burnham is facing calls from trade unions and opposition parties to ramp up North Sea production. Some Labour MPs say the oil and gas industry, centred around Aberdeen, could face collapse without new investment.

Sally Jameson, a Cabinet Office minister, has also argued that more domestic production of oil and gas would give Britain greater control over the cost of energy. Others fear it would have no real impact on bills, while wreaking untold damage on the climate.

Mike Reader, part of the Labour Environment Campaign, said there was no evidence new drilling would save jobs in the long term.

The Guardian revealed that only 27 direct full-time jobs would be created by Jackdaw, one of the biggest gasfields remaining in the North Sea, according to an environmental impact assessment filed publicly by Adura.

Ed Miliband, the new foreign secretary, previously described the Rosebank proposals as “climate vandalism” when Labour was in opposition. However, in recent weeks talks are believed to have taken place on how to allow new drilling without breaching Labour’s 2024 manifesto commitments, in which it pledged not to issue new licences but honour existing ones.

Several environmental groups are understood to be considering whether they would have grounds to take legal action regarding any government decision to allow new drilling.

Angeliki Papantoniou, a lecturer in environmental law at the University of Hull, said that, while a fresh challenge would be a “long shot”, it would be most likely to succeed if based on “substantive environmental matters” such as the disruption of ecosystems, pollution and potential health impacts.

“It could be argued that those developments cannot reasonably be ignored when taking a decision with likely high environmental effects,” she said.

“In theory, it could be hard for [Fahnbulleh] to claim that [the government] took all necessary precautionary measures without detailed risk assessments on the effects of drilling on the marine environment, climate and human health.”

Areeba Hamid, co-executive director of Greenpeace, which challenged the original decision to grant licences, said approval for the fields would make “zero difference” to energy bills and generate few jobs.

“Despite these meagre benefits, we would be prolonging a polluting industry that’s fuelling heatwaves while sending a disastrous signal to our international allies,” she said.

Odfjell Drilling declined to comment. Adura did not respond to a request for comment.

title: LeBron James, Bronny James are ‘not a package deal’ after 76ers move, agent Rich Paul says
excerpt: Victor Wembanyama is coming off a disappointing NBA Finals, and Tracy McGrady said that this will motivate him to sweep the NBA Awards in 2026/27. Nick Wright, Chris Broussard, and Kevin Wildes ask if...
body_text:
Victor Wembanyama is coming off a disappointing NBA Finals, and Tracy McGrady said that this will motivate him to sweep the NBA Awards in 2026/27. Nick Wright, Chris Broussard, and Kevin Wildes ask if Wemby will dominate the NBA, and if LeBron James going to the Warriors makes sense.

LeBron James has made what he promised to be his "last decision." Now, the focus turns to the next step in Bronny James’ young NBA career.

Bronny James' status with the Los Angeles Lakers became clear in late June, when his $2.3 million salary for next season became fully guaranteed after the team declined to waive him before the deadline. A day later, LeBron James informed the Lakers he planned to continue his career elsewhere in what will be an unprecedented 24th NBA season.

Los Angeles Lakers forward LeBron James interacts with son Bronny James during a game against the Boston Celtics at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, California, on Jan. 23, 2025. (Kirby Lee/Imagn Images)

Bronny was drafted by the Lakers in 2024 and went on to become part of the first father-son duo in NBA history. LeBron has not shied away from much it meant to share an NBA locker room with Bronny, a milestone that became even more significant when they played together in competitive games later into this past season. That history made it natural for some to wonder whether the James family would want that connection to continue.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

But Rich Paul, the CEO of Klutch Sports and the agent who represents both players, cautioned that LeBron’s decision does not mean Bronny will make a uniform change.

"They are not a package deal," Paul told ESPN. The report added there is "no current plan or request for Bronny Janes to join his father."

LeBron James (23) of the Los Angeles Lakers looks on against the Golden State Warriors during a timeout in the second half of a preseason NBA game at Chase Center on Oct. 5, 2025, in San Francisco, California. (Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images)

PHILADELPHIA ATHLETES, INCLUDING NEW TEAMMATES, REACT TO LEBRON JAMES JOINING 76ERS: 'WELCOME TO THE CITY'

All signs now point to the Lakers keeping Bronny James in Los Angeles and allowing him to continue developing under head coach J.J. Redick. The backcourt will be led by Luka Doncic, with Austin Reaves expected to remain a key piece.

Bronny will also have several young players and offseason additions around him as the Lakers reshape the roster. Adou Thiero and Dalton Knecht are set to return, while center Walker Kessler and free-agent additions Sandro Mamukelashvili, Quentin Grimes and Collin Sexton could also factor into the rotation.

Bronny James (9) and LeBron James (23) of the Los Angeles Lakers interact during a game against the Utah Jazz on April 12, 2026, at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, California. (Adam Pantozzi/NBAE via Getty Images)

Bronny appeared in 42 games last season, an increase from the 27 times he played in a game at the NBA level during his rookie campaign. He averaged 2.9 points per game in 2025-26.

Two of James’ former teams, the Cleveland Cavaliers and Miami Heat, had been floated as possible landing spots for the 41-year-old, four-time NBA champion. James said in a statement posted to social media that his decision came down to his pursuit of a fifth NBA title.

"This is my last decision. I’m not going for money. I’m not going for family. What am I really playing for at this point? I still want to sacrifice. I still want to work. I still want to grind. I still want to compete, to win and to have a chance at the feeling of winning another championship," James wrote on X.

"I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team and I am so excited to energize a new fan base and start this incredible journey one last time. Thank you LA. Miami I’ll forever love and Northeast Ohio will always home!"

Follow Fox News Digital’s sports coverage on X, and subscribe to the Fox News Sports Huddle newsletter.

Chantz Martin is a sports writer for Fox News Digital.

title: F1 needs better balance between business and sport, says Norris
excerpt:
Formula One has been driven too much by business decisions and needs to remember it is a sport, according to McLaren’s world champion Lando Norris.

With drivers chafing ⁠at new regulations that have ...
body_text:
Formula One has been driven too much by business decisions and needs to remember it is a sport, according to McLaren’s world champion Lando Norris.

With drivers chafing ⁠at new regulations that have cramped their speed, particularly at last weekend’s Belgian Grand Prix, the Briton told reporters ahead of Sunday’s Hungarian round that Formula One could do better.

“It’s a business,” said the Briton. “Everyone wants to make money, so in order for Audi ⁠and other teams to come in we had to change these things. It’s a shame. It should never have been like that. But that’s how businesses work.”

Audi have entered the sport this season after taking over Swiss-based Sauber, with the German carmaker encouraged by new rules that have increased the electrical element of the power unit to near-parity with the internal combustion engine. The rules have been ‌tweaked for 2027 to reduce the electrical contribution.

“Formula One will always be great,” said Norris, whose car has a Mercedes engine. “It can just be better.

“Us as drivers just know it better than everyone else. The thing that’s a shame is that Formula One is too heavily led by the fact it’s a business nowadays and not how can you make the sport the best possible. It’s ‘how can you just make the most money as a business?’

“And that’s just not what it should simply be. That’s not how a sport should be run. The fact we have hybrids, 50-50 and all that, that’s just because ⁠more teams wanted to come in it and because you make more money.”

Norris said the ⁠Liberty Media-owned sport was also divided between fans who followed Formula One before the arrival of the popular Netflix docu-series “Drive to Survive” and those who have been drawn to it since.

“I think the fans you have nowadays, because they’re a lot more personality-based … and not simply of Formula One as a whole ⁠sport, I think there’s less interest in basically how the actual race goes, and more just ‘has the driver done well or not?'” he added.

“I think that’s just how the fans have changed over ⁠time, and that’s completely fine. But the biggest voice should always be ours ⁠as drivers … We have the best idea of how racing should be, how it can be, what’s possible, what’s not.

“We would just want the best for everything, the best for the fans, the best viewing, the best racing for us, the most fun to drive. And at the minute, we don’t … we have very, very ‌little say, and a lot more of it’s done because if you can have Audi and other teams in it, it’s a bigger win than the drivers being happy.”

A Formula One spokesman responded to Norris’s comments by saying drivers were listened to more ‌than ‌ever.

“The sport on track is, and always will be, the priority,” he said. “Everyone has benefitted from the commercial success of Formula One, the drivers included. Decisions are made for the best strategic outcome for everyone: the fans, teams and partners.”

Norris was ⁠fastest in final ⁠practice for the Hungarian Grand Prix on Saturday.

Last year’s race winner lapped the Hungaroring circuit with ⁠a best time of 1:17.939, 0.117 seconds quicker than Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton.

Formula One championship leader Kimi ⁠Antonelli was third fastest, 0.129 seconds off the pace and ahead of Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc, McLaren’s Oscar Piastri and Mercedes teammate George Russell.

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen was seventh on the timesheets, ‌with teammate Isack Hadjar eighth but 1.004 off the pace.

title: Christian university aims to produce 'irreplaceable' graduates as AI reshapes higher education
excerpt: The Trump administration advocates for expanded AI education to build a future-ready workforce. Purdue University leads the nation by implementing AI graduation requirements, preparing students like R...
body_text:
The Trump administration advocates for expanded AI education to build a future-ready workforce. Purdue University leads the nation by implementing AI graduation requirements, preparing students like Reagan Koester for evolving industries.

Colleges and universities across the country are scrambling to respond to the rapid adoption of artificial intelligence. One Christian university is looking to embrace the technology and graduate students who are "irreplaceable." Cornerstone University wants to show other higher education institutions that the goal shouldn't be keeping AI out of the classroom, but rather help students learn to use it wisely.

"We want to lead," Cornerstone University President Gerson Moreno-Riaño told Fox News Digital. "We want to be ahead of other institutions, but we need the insight of experts in the marketplace right now that can give us guidance, direction and insight to do this and to do it well."

Cornerstone University, located in Grand Rapids, Michigan, recently announced the President’s Artificial Intelligence Advisory Board. The board is made up of experts in several fields, including philosophy, engineering, enterprise AI, theology and higher education. The members are tasked with advising Cornerstone on AI curriculum, ethics and long-term strategy.

HUMANOID ROBOT NAMED 'GABI' ORDAINED AS BUDDHIST MONK, PLEDGES DEVOTION TO 'HOLY BUDDHA'

Cornerstone University, a Christian school, is looking to tackle the question of how students use artificial intelligence responsibly. (Don Wu via iStock/Getty Images Plus)

Moreno-Riaño said the board was formed to ensure that Cornerstone's curriculum keeps pace with the rapidly evolving AI landscape, help faculty adapt to the technology and ensure the university's approach remains grounded in its Christian values.

Top universities across the country are taking different approaches to AI as the technology becomes more widely available. However, many do not have school-wide policies and instead ask faculty to use their discretion in their classrooms.

Harvard University does not have a university-wide policy regarding AI, but instead requires instructors to inform students of their policies. The university has three examples of policies that faculty can use, but it also allows them to make their own guidance. One policy prohibits the use of generative AI, such as ChatGPT, in all stages of work, while another encourages students to "explore" the limits of the tech.

Cornerstone University is looking to lead the way as higher education grapples with the challenge of how to approach AI. (Cornerstone University)

AI CHATBOTS TAKE HEAT OVER LEFT-WING BIAS: ‘NO LONGER BE CONSIDERED NEUTRAL’

Vanderbilt University also encourages faculty to establish their own generative AI use policies for their courses, as long as they align with the school's Honor Code. While the university does not have a blanket policy on generative AI, it holds faculty members responsible for clearly articulating their expectations to their students.

Moreno-Riaño said that kind of fragmented approach is exactly what Cornerstone is hoping to avoid.

"I've spoken to many college presidents and experts and have a sense that many universities right now don't know what to do with artificial intelligence," he said. "They lack a coherent strategy and focus, and what happens is that both the students suffer, and the faculty and the staff suffer. There's no guidance and direction."

"So, we want to ensure that we prepare and develop our faculty well, our staff well too, to how do we engage this in a way that continues to form our students, not just inform them. And prepare them with wisdom, not just information," he added.

The Cornerstone president also said that higher education institutions are too often focused on the potential risks of students using AI to cheat, rather than trying to teach them how to use it responsibly. Moreno-Riaño suggested that many higher education professionals who ban AI because of potential cheating are not approaching the technology in the right way. He acknowledged the negatives of AI, but said that those who are only focused on the bad, have failed to see how it can be used for good.

"Our job in academia is to prepare our faculty and ultimately our students to be able to use it with discernment and for institutions to use it to extend the reach of what they're accomplishing and quite frankly, lower the costs of what it takes to deliver an education," he said.

Cornerstone University President Dr. Gerson Moreno-Riaño aims to create "irreplaceable" graduates in the age of AI. (Getty Images)

KEY TRUMP AGENCY PUTS TOP UNIVERSITIES IN CROSSHAIRS OVER ALLEGED RACE-BASED DORM PROGRAMS

As AI becomes more capable and accessible, the conversation surrounding its relationship with higher education has expanded beyond the classroom. Students and parents are increasingly questioning which degrees and career paths will be valuable as AI reshapes the modern workforce. However, Moreno-Riaño believes they're asking the wrong question, saying that AI will change nearly every profession.

"I don't think there's a safe career or a safe diploma, a safe major. I think every field will be significantly transformed by this. But I think the question we should be asking is that we should think about producing graduates that can't be replaced," Moreno-Riaño told Fox News Digital.

For the Cornerstone president, it comes down to producing graduates who are "irreplaceable" in their fields. He argued that this does not necessarily mean teaching them to code or to focus on career paths that are AI-driven or resistant; rather, it requires universities to nourish the aspects of their students' humanity that cannot be replicated.

"I think careers are going to be transformed and changed. There's no doubt about it," he said. "But it's a human capability for wisdom and discernment that can't be replaced."

Moreno-Riaño said that students do not become wiser just by memorizing the correct answer to a question, arguing that the process played an important role in their development. He recalled a high school math teacher who insisted that students show every part of their work rather than simply writing the answer.

"The dilemma with AI is it gives you the right answer, but robs you from the struggle," he said.

Moreno-Riaño argued that the struggle to solve problems, work through mistakes and develop judgment, is ultimately what produces "irreplaceable" graduates. He added that universities should use AI to enhance students' learning experiences with the aim of helping them develop wisdom, something he thinks will be key as people question the value of a college degree in the AI age.

"Faculty need to be sources of wisdom for our students," he said.

What makes Cornerstone's approach unique, according to Moreno-Riaño, is the university's efforts to adapt to cutting-edge technology while also staying true to its Christian values.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

"I think Christianity has so much to offer here to say, we understand what the person is, we're image bearers of God, this means something," he told Fox News Digital. He added that America's founders understood this principle, which he says still sits "at the core of Christianity and of Christian higher ed."

Ultimately, Moreno-Riaño believes universities should not resist AI and instead must find ways to ensure that AI remains a tool that serves people rather than replacing them.

"It's here to stay," he said. "Now we have to learn how to use it and ensure that it serves our good purposes, not that we serve its purposes."

Rachel Wolf is a media and culture reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: What happened to Michelle Hadley? 5 things to know about ‘A Toxic Love Story’ case
